children.title: Randomized Threshold Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding driven by randomly selected threshold values or threshold regions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(\mathbb P(X_i=1)=x_i\) and \(\mathbb P(X_i=X_j=1)=\min\{x_i,x_j\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-threshold rounding of a fractional binary vector; this is a dependent, marginal-preserving coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\in[0,1]^n\), sample one variable \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and set \(X_i=\mathbf 1\{U\le x_i\}\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Return \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\). Then each coordinate has the prescribed marginal \(\mathbb P(X_i=1)=x_i\). Moreover, for every pair \(i,j\), the common threshold gives \(\mathbb P(X_i=X_j=1)=\min\{x_i,x_j\}\), so the coordinates generally are not independent. No iterative stopping test is required; the output is produced after one threshold draw and \(n\) comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw one uniform threshold and round every coordinate by whether it exceeds that threshold. Marginals are preserved, while coordinates become positively dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Threshold Rounding

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction uses one shared threshold and explicitly creates dependent coordinates, whereas the immutable path places the leaf under Independent Randomized Rounding. It therefore does not fit the exact terminal context; the taxonomy cannot be changed during statement review.

children.title: Random-Permutation Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding driven by random orderings of elements, resources, or candidate choices.

assumptions_latex: The categorical weights satisfy \(p_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_{j=1}^m p_j=1\).
The permutation \(\pi\) and threshold \(U\) are independent and uniform.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned label \(J\) satisfies \(\mathbb P(J=j)=p_j\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-transform categorical rounding after a uniformly randomized ordering of the labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(p\in\mathbb R_+^m\) with \(\sum_{j=1}^m p_j=1\), sample a uniform permutation \(\pi\) of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and independently sample \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\). Form \(s_0=0\) and \(s_r=\sum_{q=1}^r p_{\pi(q)}\). Choose the unique \(r\) satisfying \(s_{r-1}\le U<s_r\), with the final interval closed at \(1\), and return \(J=\pi(r)\). Conditional on every fixed \(\pi\), label \(j\) occupies an interval of length \(p_j\); hence \(\mathbb P(J=j)=p_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly order categorical labels, place intervals of their fractional weights in that order, and return the label containing a uniform point.
knowledge_statements.title: Random-Permutation Rounding

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The categorical inverse-transform construction is mathematically plausible, but the random permutation is distributionally unnecessary and the title has several possible meanings in approximation rounding. No cited source with a specific locator establishes that this is the intended local sense.

children.title: Distributional Coupling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Relationships between threshold distributions, ordering distributions, plus induced selections.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence forced by an almost-sure fixed sum and the limit of that implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If X\in\{0,1\}^n satisfies \sum_iX_i=k almost surely and x_i=\mathbb E[X_i], then \sum_{j\ne i}\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j)=-x_i(1-x_i). Thus nondegenerate fixed-cardinality coordinates cannot be mutually independent. Fixed cardinality alone does not imply every pairwise covariance is nonpositive: choosing \{1,2\} or \{3,4\} with equal probability has k=2 and \operatorname{Cov}(X_1,X_2)=1/4.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed total forces negative aggregate covariance around each coordinate but does not ensure pairwise negative correlation.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Cardinality Dependence Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp pairwise intersection bounds among couplings with prescribed Bernoulli marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Bernoulli variables X_i,X_j with marginals x_i,x_j, \max\{0,x_i+x_j-1\}\le\Pr(X_i=X_j=1)\le\min\{x_i,x_j\}. A common uniform threshold attains the upper bound; oppositely oriented threshold intervals attain the lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prescribed Bernoulli marginals sharply bound joint selection, with threshold constructions attaining both extremes.
knowledge_statements.title: Fréchet Bounds for Bernoulli Couplings

assumptions_latex: For the fixed-cardinality regime, \(k=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\) is an integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All three regimes preserve \(\mathbb P(X_i=1)=x_i\), but impose distinct joint laws on \(X\).

notation.meaning: set of joint laws with prescribed Bernoulli marginals
required cardinality in the fixed-sum regime

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of independent, common-threshold, and fixed-cardinality couplings with identical Bernoulli marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal C(x)=\{\mathcal L(X):X\in\{0,1\}^n,\ \mathbb P(X_i=1)=x_i\text{ for all }i\}\). The independent regime is the product law in \(\mathcal C(x)\). The common-threshold regime is represented by \(X_i=\mathbf 1\{U\le x_i\}\) using one uniform \(U\). If \(k=\sum_i x_i\in\mathbb Z\), a fixed-cardinality regime is any law in \(\mathcal C(x)\) supported on \(\{z\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i z_i=k\}\); such a law exists because \(x\) belongs to the convex hull of that set. These regimes agree on marginals but differ in dependence and support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent, shared-threshold, and fixed-cardinality couplings can preserve the same Bernoulli marginals while producing different dependence and support constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributional Coupling Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The comparison of product, common-threshold, and fixed-cardinality Bernoulli couplings is mathematically coherent, including the fixed-cardinality convex-hull claim, but no source or inspectable locator supports the representation.

children.title: Expectation-Based Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Approximation guarantees expressed through expected objective value or expected violation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected objective inequalities do not define an approximation algorithm if infeasible outputs are admitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization problem whose feasible solutions all have cost \(1\), and assign reported cost \(0\) to a designated infeasible object. An algorithm returning that object surely satisfies \(\mathbb E[C(X)]=0\le\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\) for every \(\alpha\ge1\), but returns no feasible solution. Thus an expected objective inequality is an approximation guarantee only when output feasibility is separately ensured.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low expected value attached to infeasible outputs cannot certify an approximation.
assumptions_latex: Approximation outputs are required to be feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[C(X)]\le\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\not\Rightarrow X\text{ is a valid approximation output}.
knowledge_statements.title: Output Feasibility Is Essential

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected maximization guarantee obtained from an instancewise upper benchmark.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_I\) be almost surely feasible for a maximization instance \(I\). If \(U(I)\ge\operatorname{OPT}(I)\) and \(\mathbb E[V_I(X_I)]\ge U(I)/\alpha\) for \(\alpha\ge1\), then \[\mathbb E[V_I(X_I)]\ge\frac{U(I)}{\alpha}\ge\frac{\operatorname{OPT}(I)}{\alpha}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For maximization, expected value at least one over alpha times a valid upper bound gives an expected alpha-approximation.
assumptions_latex: The randomized output is feasible almost surely.

notation.meaning: Instancewise upper bound on the maximization optimum.
Value of the randomized feasible output.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximization-Form Expected Approximation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation-only probability guarantee for a nonnegative aggregate violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(V\ge0\) is integrable and \(\mathbb E[V]\le\varepsilon\), then for every \(t>0\), \[\Pr(V\ge t)\le\frac{\varepsilon}{t}.\] In particular, \(\mathbb E[V]=0\) implies \(V=0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small expected nonnegative violation gives a Markov bound; zero expected violation gives almost-sure feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Violation Markov Guarantee

assumptions_latex: For every instance \(I\), the randomized output \(X_I\) is feasible almost surely.
For minimization, \(L(I)\le\operatorname{OPT}(I)\) and \(\mathbb E[C_I(X_I)]\le\alpha L(I)\), where \(\alpha\ge1\).

notation.meaning: cost of output on instance I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization-form expected approximation guarantee derived from a relaxation lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be any minimization instance, let \(X_I\) be an almost surely feasible randomized output, and let \(C_I(X_I)\) denote its cost. Suppose \(L(I)\le\operatorname{OPT}(I)\) and, for some \(\alpha\ge1\), \(\mathbb E[C_I(X_I)]\le\alpha L(I)\). Then \[\mathbb E[C_I(X_I)]\le\alpha L(I)\le\alpha\operatorname{OPT}(I).\] Thus the rounding procedure is an \(\alpha\)-approximation in expectation on every instance for which the two hypotheses hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If expected rounded cost is at most alpha times a valid relaxation lower bound, then it is at most alpha times the optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Expectation-Based Guarantees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimization inequality and theorem role are correct, but the record supplies no citation with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator. The local inventory does not contain an evident source for this approximation guarantee.

children.title: Averaging Arguments
children.top_down_role: Existence arguments derived from averages over outcomes, choices, or parameter values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Averaging over a Finite Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branchwise averaging over positive-probability cells.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be integrable and let \(A_1,\ldots,A_r\) be a finite measurable partition. Then \[\mathbb E[Z]=\sum_{j:\Pr(A_j)>0}\Pr(A_j)\mathbb E[Z\mid A_j].\] Consequently, some positive-probability cell has conditional mean at most \(\mathbb E[Z]\), and some such cell has conditional mean at least \(\mathbb E[Z]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global expectation is a weighted average of supported branch expectations, so a branch exists on each side of the average.

notation.meaning: Cell of the finite measurable partition.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Averaging over a Finite Partition

assumptions_latex: The real random variable \(Z\) is integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists an outcome \(\omega\) with \(Z(\omega)\le B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary averaging principle in the upper-bound form used for minimization objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be an integrable real random variable on a nonempty probability space. If \(\mathbb E[Z]\le B\), then the event that every outcome has value strictly greater than \(B\) is impossible. Consequently, there exists an outcome \(\omega\) in the support of the experiment such that \(Z(\omega)\le B\). For a finite sample space with probabilities \(p_s\), this is equivalently the assertion that \(\sum_s p_s Z(s)\le B\) implies \(\min_{s:p_s>0}Z(s)\le B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An average no greater than a bound guarantees at least one positively weighted outcome whose value is no greater than that bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Averaging Arguments

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The averaging principle is standard, but no source is cited. Moreover, 'support of the experiment' is not defined for the stated arbitrary probability space; the finite positive-mass formulation is precise, while the general formulation should be source-aligned or stated in almost-sure terms.

children.title: Instancewise Extraction Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Passage from aggregate probabilistic guarantees to a qualifying solution for a fixed instance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Las Vegas extraction from a randomized generator with a verifiable qualifying event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each independent trial generate \(X\), and let a deterministic verifier recognize a qualifying event \(G(X)\). If \(\Pr(G(X))\ge q>0\), repeatedly generate and verify trials until one qualifies. The returned output satisfies \(G\), and the trial count \(T\) obeys \[\Pr(T>t)\le(1-q)^t\le e^{-qt},\qquad \mathbb E[T]\le1/q.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly sample and verify until success; a positive success bound gives a Las Vegas output with geometric trial bounds.
assumptions_latex: The verifier is sound and complete for \(G\).
A one-trial lower bound \(q>0\) is known.

notation.meaning: Number of trials through the first success.

knowledge_statements.title: Verified Rejection Extraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic extraction by enumerating a finite positive-probability support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an experiment has finite support \(S\), probabilities \(p_s>0\), and evaluable costs \(C(s)\). Enumerate \(S\) and return \(s^*\in\arg\min_{s\in S}C(s)\). Then \[C(s^*)\le\sum_{s\in S}p_sC(s)=\mathbb E[C(X)].\] If evaluating outcome \(s\) costs \(T_s\), the total work is \(O(\sum_{s\in S}T_s)\), apart from enumeration overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerating the support and taking its cheapest outcome deterministically realizes the averaging guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The positive-probability support is finite and enumerable.
Every supported outcome can be evaluated.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit-Support Best-Outcome Extraction
Instancewise Extraction Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-of-conditional-expectations interface for extracting a deterministic realization from finitely supported random decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) be finite-valued random decisions and let \(Z=g(R_1,\ldots,R_m)\) be integrable. Starting with no decisions fixed, for each \(i\in\{1,ldots,m\}\), choose a value \(r_i\) having positive conditional probability given the previously selected prefix and minimizing \(\mathbb E[Z\mid R_1=r_1,\ldots,R_i=r_i]\) over all such values. After all decisions are fixed, return \((r_1,\ldots,r_m)\). The resulting realization satisfies \(g(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\le\mathbb E[Z]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely supported random decisions, fix each decision sequentially to a conditionally supported value minimizing the remaining expected cost. The final deterministic cost is no greater than the original expectation.
assumptions_latex: The decisions \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) are finite-valued and determine an integrable cost \(Z=g(R_1,\ldots,R_m)\).
At every reachable prefix, the relevant conditional expectations can be computed and a minimizing conditionally supported value can be selected.

notation.meaning: integrable cost determined by all decisions
cost function of the completed decisions

children.title: Chernoff-Type Concentration
children.top_down_role: Multiplicative or exponential tail controls for sums arising in randomized rounding.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginals Alone Do Not Imply Chernoff Concentration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence boundary for randomized-rounding applications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X_1=\cdots=X_n=Y\) with \(Y\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\), then every \(X_i\) has marginal \(p\), but \(S=nY\) satisfies \(\mathbb P(S=n)=p\). Thus matching independent-rounding marginals without independence or suitable negative dependence does not imply an exponentially small upper tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly correlated indicators show that preserved marginals alone do not give Chernoff concentration.
assumptions_latex: All indicators equal one shared Bernoulli variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Chernoff tails cannot be inferred solely from individual marginals.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginals Alone Do Not Imply Chernoff Concentration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard closed-form consequences of the exact Bernoulli-sum rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an independent Bernoulli sum \(S\) with mean \(\mu\), \[\mathbb P\{S\ge(1+\delta)\mu\}\le e^{-\mu\delta^2/(2+\delta)}\quad(\delta\ge0),\] and \[\mathbb P\{S\le(1-\delta)\mu\}\le e^{-\mu\delta^2/2}\quad(0\le\delta\le1).\] In particular, the upper tail is at most \(e^{-\mu\delta^2/3}\) for \(0\le\delta\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact Chernoff rate implies familiar quadratic multiplicative bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a sum of independent Bernoulli variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed simplified upper- and lower-tail bounds hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplified Multiplicative Chernoff Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence-compatible extension used by negatively dependent rounding schemes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_i\in\{0,1\}\), \(p_i=\mathbb EX_i\), \(S=\sum_iX_i\), and \(\mu=\sum_i p_i\). If \(\mathbb E\prod_{i\in A}X_i\le\prod_{i\in A}p_i\) for every \(A\), then the independent-Bernoulli upper-tail Chernoff bound holds. If also \(\mathbb E\prod_{i\in A}(1-X_i)\le\prod_{i\in A}(1-p_i)\), then the corresponding lower-tail bound holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper and lower cylinder inequalities can replace full independence for Chernoff tails of indicator sums.
assumptions_latex: The upper-cylinder inequality holds for upper tails; the lower-cylinder inequality additionally holds for lower tails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The standard Bernoulli-sum Chernoff upper and corresponding lower bounds remain valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Chernoff Bounds Under Cylinder Dependence

assumptions_latex: The variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are independent and take values in \(\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative Chernoff bounds for an independent, not necessarily identically distributed, Bernoulli sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be independent Bernoulli variables, set \(S=\sum_{i=1}^nX_i\), and write \(\mu=\mathbb E[S]\). For every \(\delta\ge0\), \[\mathbb P\{S\ge(1+\delta)\mu\}\le\left(\frac{e^\delta}{(1+\delta)^{1+\delta}}\right)^\mu.\] For every \(\delta\in[0,1]\), \[\mathbb P\{S\le(1-\delta)\mu\}\le\exp\left(-\frac{\mu\delta^2}{2}\right).\] These statements also cover unequal success probabilities through \(\mu=\sum_i\mathbb E[X_i]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent Bernoulli sums have exponentially small upper and lower multiplicative tails, governed by their mean and relative deviation.
knowledge_statements.title: Chernoff-Type Concentration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated multiplicative Chernoff bounds are standard and correctly restricted to independent Bernoulli variables, but no authoritative citation or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Poisson-Type Concentration
children.top_down_role: Tail controls reflecting sparse-event or Poisson-like occupancy behavior.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Poisson-Rate Exponent Does Not Imply a Poisson Law
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates concentration with a Poisson rate from distributional Poisson approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Bernoulli sum may satisfy a tail inequality with exponent \(\mu h(t/\mu)\) while being far from \(\operatorname{Poisson}(\mu)\). For example, a Bernoulli variable with success probability one is deterministic, whereas \(\operatorname{Poisson}(1)\) is not. Thus a Poisson-rate concentration bound alone gives no distributional Poisson approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sharing the Poisson large-deviation exponent does not imply sharing the Poisson distribution.
assumptions_latex: Only a Poisson-rate tail inequality is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A separate approximation hypothesis is required to conclude closeness to a Poisson law.
knowledge_statements.title: Poisson-Rate Exponent Does Not Imply a Poisson Law

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-deviation-rate inequalities for an actual Poisson random variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(N\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(\mu)\), \(\mu>0\), then for \(t\ge0\), \[\mathbb P\{N\ge\mu+t\}\le\exp[-\mu h(t/\mu)],\qquad h(u)=(1+u)\log(1+u)-u.\] For \(0\le t\le\mu\), \[\mathbb P\{N\le\mu-t\}\le\exp[-\mu h(-t/\mu)],\qquad h(-u)=(1-u)\log(1-u)+u.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Poisson variable has upper and lower tails governed by its relative-entropy rate function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed upper- and lower-tail rate bounds hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Poisson Rate Bounds

assumptions_latex: The variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are independent Bernoulli variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The upper tail obeys \(\mathbb P(S\ge\mu+t)\le\exp[-\mu h(t/\mu)]\), where \(h(u)=(1+u)\log(1+u)-u\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Poisson-rate upper-tail inequality for a Poisson-binomial sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be independent Bernoulli variables, let \(S=\sum_{i=1}^nX_i\), and suppose \(\mu=\mathbb E[S]>0\). Define \(h(u)=(1+u)\log(1+u)-u\) for \(u\ge0\). Then, for every \(t\ge0\), \[\mathbb P\{S\ge\mu+t\}\le\exp\left[-\mu h\left(\frac{t}{\mu}\right)\right].\] The exponent is the same rate function obtained from the moment-generating function of a Poisson random variable of mean \(\mu\), although \(S\) itself need not be Poisson.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bernoulli sum has an upper-tail bound with the Poisson large-deviation rate function, even when its success probabilities differ.
knowledge_statements.title: Poisson-Type Concentration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional approximation rather than a concentration theorem; canonical home lies in Poisson approximation theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For independent \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_i)\), a standard Le Cam bound controls the total-variation distance between \(\sum_iX_i\) and \(\operatorname{Poisson}(\sum_i p_i)\) by a constant-convention-dependent multiple of \(\sum_i p_i^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse independent Bernoulli sums admit Poisson distributional approximation.

children.title: Tail-Regime Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Relative suitability of concentration families across deviation scales plus sparsity regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent additive-scale interpretation of the Poisson-Chernoff rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Writing \(t=\mu\delta\), \[\mu h(t/\mu)=\Theta(t^2/\mu)\quad\text{when }t=o(\mu),\] while \[\mu h(t/\mu)=\Theta\!\left(t\log(t/\mu)\right)\quad\text{when }t/\mu\to\infty.\] Thus moderate deviations have Gaussian scale, whereas deviations far above the mean have Poisson large-deviation scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In additive units, moderate deviations have a quadratic exponent and far-upper-tail deviations have a t log(t/mu) exponent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed moderate- and large-deviation asymptotics hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive-Deviation Regime Translation

assumptions_latex: An upper tail is bounded by \(\exp[-\mu h(\delta)]\) with \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small- and large-deviation comparison of the exact Chernoff rate with a Bernstein simplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h(\delta)=(1+\delta)\log(1+\delta)-\delta\), \[h(\delta)\ge\frac{\delta^2}{2+2\delta/3}\qquad(\delta\ge0).\] Hence a bound \(\exp[-\mu h(\delta)]\) is at least as strong as \(\exp[-\mu\delta^2/(2+2\delta/3)]\). Moreover, \(h(\delta)=\delta^2/2+O(\delta^3)\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\), giving Gaussian-scale moderate deviations, whereas \(h(\delta)=\delta\log\delta+O(\delta)\) as \(\delta\to\infty\), giving a stronger large-deviation exponent than a purely quadratic-over-linear simplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact Poisson-Chernoff rate is quadratic for small relative deviations and grows like delta log delta for large deviations.
knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Regime Comparisons

children.title: Bounded-Difference Concentration
children.top_down_role: Concentration interfaces based on limited sensitivity to individual random choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for the independent-coordinate bounded-difference theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), set \(Y_i=Y\) for all \(i\), and let \(f(y)=\sum_i y_i\). Changing one coordinate changes \(f\) by at most one, but \[\mathbb P\{f(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)-\mathbb Ef\ge n/2\}=1/2,\] whereas the independent-input formula would give \(e^{-n/2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate sensitivity alone does not imply McDiarmid concentration for dependent coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_1=\cdots=Y_n\) is one shared fair Bernoulli variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The independent-input McDiarmid bound may fail under dependence.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure Without Independence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-moment form underlying McDiarmid's tail inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the independent-coordinate bounded-difference assumptions, \[\mathbb E\exp\!\left(\lambda(f(Y)-\mathbb Ef(Y))\right)\le\exp\!\left(\frac{\lambda^2}{8}\sum_i c_i^2\right)\qquad(\lambda\in\mathbb R).\] Optimizing the exponential Markov bound yields \(\mathbb P(f(Y)-\mathbb Ef(Y)\ge t)\le e^{-2t^2/\sum_i c_i^2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded-difference function of independent inputs is sub-Gaussian with squared-sensitivity parameter.
assumptions_latex: Replacing coordinate \(i\) changes \(f\) by at most \(c_i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sub-Gaussian Moment-Generating Form

assumptions_latex: Changing only coordinate \(i\) changes \(f\) by at most \(c_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(t\ge0\), \(\mathbb P(f(Y)-\mathbb E f(Y)\ge t)\le\exp[-2t^2/\sum_i c_i^2]\), with the same bound for the lower tail.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: McDiarmid's inequality for independent inputs with deterministic coordinate sensitivities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) be independent variables and let \(f\) be measurable. Assume that whenever \(y\) and \(y'\) differ only in coordinate \(i\), \(|f(y)-f(y')|\le c_i\). If \(f(Y)\) is integrable, then for every \(t\ge0\), \[\mathbb P\{f(Y)-\mathbb E[f(Y)]\ge t\}\le\exp\left(-\frac{2t^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n c_i^2}\right).\] The identical bound holds for \(\mathbb P\{\mathbb E[f(Y)]-f(Y)\ge t\}\), and a union bound gives a two-sided prefactor of \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function of independent variables concentrates around its mean when replacing one coordinate can change its value only by a bounded amount.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Difference Concentration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is a correctly scoped form of McDiarmid's bounded-difference inequality, but no authoritative source with a theorem, section, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Martingale Concentration
children.top_down_role: Concentration interfaces based on sequentially revealed conditional information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Sub-Gaussian Tail From Martingality Alone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for applying Azuma-type conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_0=0\) and \(M_1=X\), where \(X\) is an integrable mean-zero random variable with a polynomial tail. Then \((M_0,M_1)\) is a martingale, but \(\mathbb P(|M_1-M_0|\ge t)\) need not decay sub-Gaussianly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-step heavy-tailed martingale shows that martingality alone gives no Azuma-type tail.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is integrable and has a polynomial tail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No universal bound Ce^{-ct^2}\text{ follows from martingality alone}.
knowledge_statements.title: No Sub-Gaussian Tail From Martingality Alone

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided martingale tail controlled by predictable quadratic variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_k=M_k-M_{k-1}\) satisfy \(D_k\le b\) almost surely, where \(b>0\), and define \(V_n=\sum_{k=1}^n\mathbb E[D_k^2\mid\mathcal F_{k-1}]\). For \(t,v>0\), \[\mathbb P\{M_n-M_0\ge t\text{ and }V_n\le v\}\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2(v+bt/3)}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Freedman's inequality uses predictable quadratic variation with a bounded-increment correction.
assumptions_latex: \(D_k\le b\) almost surely for a deterministic \(b>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Freedman Variance-Sensitive Concentration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Martingale concentration using deterministic increment ranges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((M_k,\mathcal F_k)\) be a martingale. Suppose deterministic constants \(a_k\le b_k\) satisfy \(a_k\le M_k-M_{k-1}\le b_k\) almost surely. Then for every \(t\ge0\), \[\mathbb P\{M_n-M_0\ge t\}\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{2t^2}{\sum_{k=1}^n(b_k-a_k)^2}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A martingale with deterministic bounded increment ranges has a Gaussian tail governed by the squared range lengths.
assumptions_latex: The deterministic bounds \(a_k,b_k\) contain the kth increment almost surely.

notation.meaning: deterministic lower and upper increment bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Hoeffding–Azuma Bounded-Range Variant

assumptions_latex: The process \((M_k,\mathcal F_k)_{k=0}^n\) is a martingale.
Its increments satisfy \(|M_k-M_{k-1}|\le c_k\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Azuma-Hoeffding concentration for a martingale with bounded absolute increments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((M_k,\mathcal F_k)_{k=0}^n\) be a real-valued martingale. Suppose deterministic constants \(c_k\ge0\) satisfy \(|M_k-M_{k-1}|\le c_k\) almost surely for every \(k\). Then, for every \(t\ge0\), \[\mathbb P\{M_n-M_0\ge t\}\le\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sum_{k=1}^n c_k^2}\right).\] Applying the same inequality to \(-M_k\) gives \[\mathbb P\{|M_n-M_0|\ge t\}\le2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sum_{k=1}^n c_k^2}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A martingale whose increments are uniformly bounded has Gaussian-type terminal tails controlled by the sum of squared increment bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Martingale Concentration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Azuma-Hoeffding bounds and theorem classification are appropriate, but the candidate has no citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Exposure-Sequence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Choices of reveal order, filtration, plus dependency granularity in rounding analysis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable interface between a reveal scheme and bounded-increment concentration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every history through stage \(k-1\), suppose the possible values of \(\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F_k]\) over next-stage outcomes consistent with that history lie in an interval of length at most a deterministic constant \(c_k\). Then the Doob increment satisfies \(|M_k-M_{k-1}|\le c_k\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform conditional-expectation range bound yields a valid Doob-increment bound.
assumptions_latex: For every relevant history, the next-stage conditional-expectation range has length at most deterministic \(c_k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Range Increment Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison among exposure schemes for the same terminal random variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Different reveal orders or blockings can have the same endpoints \(M_0=\mathbb EZ\) and \(M_n=Z\) while yielding different valid increment or conditional-variance bounds. Thus the resulting concentration parameter, such as \(\sum_k c_k^2\), need not be invariant under the exposure scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reveal order and granularity leave the target unchanged but can change the quality of its concentration bound.
assumptions_latex: The stated increment or variance controls are valid for their respective schemes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_0\text{ and }M_n\text{ are invariant, but the concentration parameters need not be invariant}.
knowledge_statements.title: Reveal-Order and Blocking Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates martingality from assumptions used to bound increments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any integrable \(Z\) and increasing filtration \(\mathcal F_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal F_n\), the process \(M_k=\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F_k]\) is a martingale. Independence of exposed coordinates is unnecessary for this identity; it is an additional condition often used to control the increments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional expectations form a Doob martingale under arbitrary dependence.
knowledge_statements.title: General Doob Exposure Construction

assumptions_latex: The independent variables \(Y_1,ldots,Y_n\) determine an integrable variable \(Z=f(Y_1,ldots,Y_n)\).
An ordering \(\pi\) specifies the sequence in which coordinates are revealed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exposure process \(M_k=\mathbb E[Z\mid Y_{\pi(1)},ldots,Y_{\pi(k)}]\) is a martingale ending at \(Z\), and valid increment bounds yield martingale concentration.

notation.meaning: quantity determined by all exposed variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Doob-martingale construction induced by revealing independent random choices in a chosen order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) be independent, let \(Z=f(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)\) be integrable, and fix a permutation \(\pi\). Define \(\mathcal F_k=\sigma(Y_{\pi(1)},\ldots,Y_{\pi(k)})\) and \(M_k=\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F_k]\). Then \((M_k,\mathcal F_k)_{k=0}^n\) is a martingale with \(M_0=\mathbb E[Z]\) and \(M_n=Z\) almost surely. Consequently, any deterministic or predictable bounds established for the exposure increments \(M_k-M_{k-1}\) can be inserted into an appropriate martingale concentration inequality; the ordering may affect those bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reveal independent choices in a selected order and track the conditional expectation. This produces a martingale whose increment bounds control the final deviation.
knowledge_statements.title: Exposure-Sequence Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Doob exposure-martingale construction is correct and the principle role fits the container, but the assumptions contain repeated missing backslashes before \ldots and no source with a specific locator is cited.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent-trial amplification of a union-bound feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If one trial is feasible with probability at least \(\delta>0\), then among \(t\) independent trials the probability that none is feasible is at most \[(1-\delta)^t\le e^{-\delta t}.\] Hence \[t\ge\left\lceil\frac{\ln(1/\eta)}{\delta}\right\rceil\] suffices for success probability at least \(1-\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent repetition amplifies a positive feasibility probability to any prescribed confidence.
assumptions_latex: Each trial is feasible with probability at least \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Repetition Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality Does Not Uniformly Certify Positive Success
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary of the union-bound positive-probability conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1=\{Z=0\}\) and \(B_2=\{Z=1\}\) for a fair bit \(Z\). Then \[\Pr(B_1)+\Pr(B_2)=1,\qquad \Pr(B_1\cup B_2)=1.\] Thus \(\sum_i\Pr(B_i)\le1\) does not uniformly imply a positive probability of avoiding every bad event. Strict inequality, equivalently explicit positive union-bound slack, is required for that certificate, although particular event families with sum one may still have positive avoidance probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At total bad-event probability exactly one, the events may cover the entire sample space, so equality gives no uniform positive-success certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality Does Not Uniformly Certify Positive Success

assumptions_latex: The bad events \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) are measurable in a common probability space.
A random rounded solution is feasible exactly when none of the events \(B_i\) occurs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(\bigcap_{i=1}^m \overline{B_i})\ge 1-\sum_{i=1}^m\Pr(B_i)\); hence \(\sum_i\Pr(B_i)<1\) implies existence of a feasible outcome.

notation.meaning: Bad event corresponding to violation of constraint i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-family union-bound criterion, including repeated-sampling feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) be the bad events produced by a randomized rounding experiment. Then
\[
\Pr\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^m B_i\right)\le \sum_{i=1}^m\Pr(B_i),
\qquad
\Pr\!\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^m\overline{B_i}\right)\ge 1-\sum_{i=1}^m\Pr(B_i).
\]
Consequently, if \(\sum_i\Pr(B_i)\le 1-\delta\) for some \(\delta>0\), a feasible rounded solution exists and one independent trial is feasible with probability at least \(\delta\). Repeating the trial until feasibility therefore uses at most \(1/\delta\) trials in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the total probability of all constraint-violation events is below one, some rounded outcome is feasible; with slack delta, independent repetition succeeds after at most 1/delta trials on average.
knowledge_statements.title: Union-Bound Feasibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem and its expected-repetition consequence are mathematically standard and fit Union-Bound Feasibility, but the record supplies no citation or inspectable locator. Source support is required before candidate-review acceptance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive variable-model local lemma with expected resampling-count bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initially sample all mutually independent variables. While some bad event \(B_i\) holds, select one and independently resample every variable determining \(B_i\). If witnesses \(x_i\in(0,1)\) satisfy \[\Pr(B_i)\le x_i\prod_{j\in\Gamma(i)}(1-x_j),\] then the procedure terminates almost surely with no bad event, and the expected number \(N_i\) of resamplings caused by \(B_i\) is at most \(x_i/(1-x_i)\). Thus \[\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_iN_i\right]\le\sum_i\frac{x_i}{1-x_i}.\] This bounds resampling steps; a wall-clock bound additionally requires costs for finding a violated event and resampling its variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resampling the variables of a currently violated event constructively realizes the variable-model local lemma with a bounded expected number of resampling steps.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many mutually independent underlying variables and finitely many bad events.
Each bad event is determined by a known finite variable set.
The displayed asymmetric witness inequalities hold.
A violated event can be selected whenever one exists.

notation.meaning: Number of resamplings triggered by bad event \(B_i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invalid Dependency Graph Can Falsify the Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary requiring the declared graph to satisfy the local lemma's independence condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be a fair bit, \(B_1=\{Z=0\}\), and \(B_2=\{Z=1\}\). If the dependency graph is incorrectly declared empty, then \(\Pr(B_i)=1/2\le x_i\) for \(x_1=x_2=3/4\), apparently satisfying the empty-neighborhood inequalities. Nevertheless \(B_1\cup B_2\) is certain and \(\Pr(\overline{B_1}\cap\overline{B_2})=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting an actual dependence can make the numerical inequalities hold although simultaneous avoidance is impossible.
assumptions_latex: The declared empty graph is invalid because both events depend on \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Dependency Graph Can Falsify the Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform probability-degree specialization of the local lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every bad event has probability at most \(p\), every event is dependent on at most \(d\) other events in a valid dependency graph, and \[ep(d+1)\le1,\] then \[\Pr\!\left(\bigcap_i\overline{B_i}\right)>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All bad events can be avoided when their probabilities and dependency degrees satisfy the symmetric local-lemma bound.
assumptions_latex: The stated graph is a valid dependency graph.
Every dependency degree is at most \(d\).
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Local-Lemma Criterion

assumptions_latex: Each bad event \(B_i\) is determined by a specified subset of the variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed local-lemma inequalities certify \(\Pr(\bigcap_i\overline{B_i})>0\) and provide the dependency interface for event-based resampling.

notation.meaning: Open neighborhood of event i in D.
Local-lemma witness assigned to event i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymmetric variable-model local-lemma interface for rounding constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) be bad events determined by independent variables \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\), and connect two events in \(D\) whenever their determining variable sets intersect. A local-lemma rounding interface is valid when there exist \(x_i\in(0,1)\) such that
\[
\Pr(B_i)\le x_i\prod_{j\in\Gamma(i)}(1-x_j)
\quad\text{for every }i.
\]
Under these inequalities, \(\Pr(\bigcap_i\overline{B_i})>0\). The event-variable incidence lists also identify which variables may be resampled when a violated event is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bad events sharing random variables form a dependency graph. Suitable local witness values certify simultaneous avoidance and identify the variables associated with each resampling repair.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Lemma Rounding Interfaces

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic characterization of deletion-only feasibility repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible family \(\mathcal F\subseteq2^E\) and initial set \(R\subseteq E\), a deletion alteration is a set \(D\in\mathcal F\) with \(D\subseteq R\). Such a repair exists exactly when \(\{F\in\mathcal F:F\subseteq R\}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deletion alteration is a feasible subset of the initially rounded set; it exists exactly when such a subset exists.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Covering Violations Are Irreparable by Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp directionality boundary for deletion-only repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(g:2^E\to\mathbb R\) is inclusion-monotone and \(g(R)<b\), then \(g(D)<b\) for every \(D\subseteq R\). Hence deletion cannot repair an already violated monotone lower-bound constraint \(g(S)\ge b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing elements cannot repair an already violated monotone lower-bound constraint.

An initial random set \(R\subseteq E\) is available.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic deletion repair for finite cardinality packing constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an initial rounded set \(R\subseteq E\) and constraints \(|S\cap C_j|\le b_j\). Initialize \(S\leftarrow R\). While some constraint \(j\) satisfies \(|S\cap C_j|>b_j\), choose such a \(j\) and delete an element \(e\in S\cap C_j\) according to the prescribed deletion rule. Stop when no constraint is violated and output \(S\). Each iteration strictly decreases \(|S|\), so the procedure terminates after at most \(|R|\) deletions; at termination every packing constraint is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a random set, repeatedly remove an element from any overfull packing constraint. The process terminates with a feasible subset after at most one deletion per initially selected element.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic augmentation repair for finite cardinality covering constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an initial rounded set \(R\subseteq E\) and constraints \(|S\cap C_j|\ge b_j\). Initialize \(S\leftarrow R\). While some \(j\) satisfies \(|S\cap C_j|<b_j\), invoke the repair oracle to choose \(e\in C_j\setminus S\) and set \(S\leftarrow S\cup\{e\}\). Stop when all constraints hold and output \(S\). Every iteration increases \(|S|\), so the procedure terminates after at most \(|E\setminus R|\) augmentations whenever the oracle can repair every encountered violation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected objective-loss accounting for deletion or augmentation repairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\) be the preliminary rounded object and \(S\) the repaired output. Suppose repair actions are indexed by \(a\), action \(a\) has indicator \(I_a\) and nonnegative charge \(c_a\), and
\[
V(S)\ge V(R)-\sum_a c_a I_a
\]
holds for every execution. Taking expectations gives
\[
\mathbb E[V(S)]\ge \mathbb E[V(R)]-\sum_a c_a\Pr(I_a=1).
\]
Thus any bounds \(\Pr(I_a=1)\le q_a\) yield the certificate \(\mathbb E[V(S)]\ge\mathbb E[V(R)]-\sum_a c_aq_a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Charge each possible repair a deterministic objective loss. The expected repaired value is at least the initial expected value minus the sum of each charge times its repair probability.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite bipartite edge rounding with marginals and degree floor-ceiling guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\in[0,1]^E\), repeatedly choose a cycle or maximal path in the subgraph of fractional edges. Partition its edges alternately into \(M_1\) and \(M_2\), and randomly move in one of the two signed directions that increases \(M_1\) while decreasing \(M_2\), or conversely. Choose maximal step lengths so that at least one edge becomes integral, and choose direction probabilities making every edge coordinate a martingale. When all coordinates are integral, output \(X\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration bound for maximal transfers between strictly fractional coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=|\{i:0<x_i<1\}|\). Repeatedly apply a maximal pairwise transfer to two strictly fractional coordinates and never update an integral coordinate. Every iteration makes at least one selected coordinate integral. If \(f\ge2\), after at most \(f-1\) iterations at most one fractional coordinate remains. If the preserved total \(\sum_i x_i\) is integral, no single fractional coordinate can remain, so the terminal vector is integral. For \(f=0\), no update is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each maximal pair update eliminates at least one fractional coordinate; an integral preserved total rules out a lone fractional remainder.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical sum-preserving two-coordinate randomized update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fractional coordinates \(x_i,x_j\), set \(a=\min\{1-x_i,x_j\}\) and \(b=\min\{x_i,1-x_j\}\). Replace \(x\) by
\[
x+a(e_i-e_j)\quad\text{with probability }\frac{b}{a+b},
\]
and by
\[
x-b(e_i-e_j)\quad\text{with probability }\frac{a}{a+b}.
\]
The new vector remains in \([0,1]^n\), preserves \(x_i+x_j\) deterministically, and preserves each updated coordinate in expectation. By maximality of \(a\) and \(b\), at least one of the two coordinates becomes integral in either outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move mass between two fractional coordinates to a maximal endpoint, choosing probabilities that preserve both expectations. Their sum stays fixed and at least one coordinate becomes integral.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Rounding

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-coordinate update is internally consistent, preserves the sum and coordinate expectations, and makes at least one coordinate integral. It fits Pairwise Rounding as an algorithm, but it has no source or specific locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex-degree guarantee for alternating bipartite dependent rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d_v(x)=\sum_{e\in\delta(v)}x_e\). Alternating cycle updates preserve \(d_v(x)\) at every incident vertex, while alternating maximal-path updates can change the residual fractional degree only at the path endpoints. When the procedure terminates at \(X\in\{0,1\}^E\), each vertex satisfies
\[
\lfloor d_v(x)\rfloor\le d_v(X)\le\lceil d_v(x)\rceil.
\]
Because \(d_v(X)\) is integral, it equals one of these two bounds. In particular, every initially integral fractional degree is preserved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent rounding changes each vertex's fractional degree only enough to reach its floor or ceiling. Any degree that starts integral is preserved exactly.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural representation of all coordinate pairs preserving a linear invariant under mass transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), define \(i\sim_A j\) if and only if \(Ae_i=Ae_j\). This is an equivalence relation. The mass-transfer directions \(e_i-e_j\) satisfying \(A(e_i-e_j)=0\) are exactly those whose endpoints lie in one equivalence class. Hence the compatibility graph is the disjoint union of cliques indexed by the distinct columns of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinates may exchange mass exactly when their columns in the invariant matrix coincide; compatible coordinates form disjoint cliques.

notation.meaning: Coordinates i and j have identical columns in A.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The invariant is preserved for every such pairwise step if and only if \(Ae_i=Ae_j\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebraic compatibility of sum-transfer pair updates with exact invariants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the current vector satisfies \(Ax=b\), and a pairwise rounding step has the form \(x'=x+t(e_i-e_j)\) for some feasible nonzero \(t\). Then
\[
Ax'=b+tA(e_i-e_j).
\]
Consequently, the linear system \(Ax=b\) is preserved for every allowed magnitude and either sign of this pairwise step if and only if
\[
A(e_i-e_j)=0,
\]
equivalently, the \(i\)-th and \(j\)-th columns of \(A\) coincide. Thus only compatible coordinate pairs may be used when exact preservation is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mass-transfer update between two coordinates preserves specified linear equalities exactly precisely when those coordinates have identical coefficient columns in the invariant system.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp cardinality control when exact preservation is arithmetically impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s=\sum_i x_i\). If a rounding process preserves the total until at most one coordinate remains fractional and then rounds that coordinate without changing its expectation, the final cardinality \(K=\sum_iX_i\) lies in \(\{\lfloor s\rfloor,\lceil s\rceil\}\) almost surely and satisfies \(\mathbb E[K]=s\). When \(s\notin\mathbb Z\), \(\Pr(K=\lceil s\rceil)=s-\lfloor s\rfloor\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonintegral total is rounded to one of its adjacent integers, and expectation preservation fixes the probability of the larger value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cardinality preservation when the initial total is integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Each pairwise update replaces two coordinates without changing their sum and leaves every other coordinate fixed. Hence the total \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\) is invariant throughout the rounding process. If the initial total is an integer \(k\) and the process terminates at \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\), then
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n X_i=k=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i
\]
holds for every execution. Equivalently, the selected set \(\{i:X_i=1\}\) has cardinality exactly \(k\), not merely expected cardinality \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because every pair update preserves the total mass, an initially integral total becomes the exact cardinality of every final integral outcome.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginals Alone Do Not Control Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of coordinatewise marginals from cardinality and correlation guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) with \(0<p<1\), and set \(X_i=Y\) for every \(i\). Then \(\mathbb E[X_i]=p\), but \(\sum_iX_i\in\{0,n\}\) and, for distinct \(i,j\), \(\Pr(X_i=X_j=1)=p>p^2\). Thus marginal preservation alone implies neither cardinality concentration nor negative correlation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise marginal preservation for a terminating dependent-rounding process.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume every rounding update satisfies
\[
\mathbb E[x_i^{(t+1)}\mid x^{(t)}]=x_i^{(t)}
\quad\text{for every }i.
\]
Thus each coordinate process is a bounded martingale. If the procedure terminates at an integral vector \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\), then
\[
\mathbb E[X_i]=x_i^{(0)}=x_i.
\]
Since \(X_i\) is binary, \(\mathbb E[X_i]=\Pr(X_i=1)\). Therefore the final random set includes element \(i\) with exactly its original fractional probability, even though different inclusion indicators may be dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every update preserves each coordinate's conditional expectation, then the final binary coordinate equals one with probability exactly its original fractional value.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Preservation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The marginal-preservation property is standard, but passage from stepwise martingale preservation to the terminal vector requires a precisely stated almost-sure termination or convergence condition. The phrase 'terminates integrably' is not sufficiently standard without a supporting source, and no citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact characterization of marginals realizable by a random fixed-cardinality subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\), a vector \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) is the marginal vector of a random \(k\)-element subset of \([n]\) if and only if \(0\le x_i\le1\) for every \(i\) and \(\sum_i x_i=k\). Equivalently, \(\{x\in[0,1]^n:\sum_i x_i=k\}=\operatorname{conv}\{\mathbf1_S:|S|=k\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Box constraints and an integral total are exactly the conditions for realizing prescribed marginals with fixed cardinality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is realizable with }|S|=k\text{ a.s.}\iff x\in[0,1]^n\text{ and }\sum_i x_i=k.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Cardinality Marginal Realizability
Joint Preservation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous cardinality and marginal guarantees for uniform-matroid dependent rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in[0,1]^n\) satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=k\) for an integer \(k\). A joint cardinality-marginal preserving rounding produces a random vector \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) such that
\[\sum_{i=1}^n X_i=k\quad\text{almost surely},\qquad \mathbb E[X_i]=x_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\]
More generally, when \(\sum_i x_i\) is not integral, the cardinality lies almost surely in \(\{\lfloor\sum_i x_i\rfloor,\lceil\sum_i x_i\rceil\}\), while every marginal remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent rounding can preserve every coordinate’s marginal while making total cardinality exact, or one of the two adjacent integers when the fractional total is nonintegral.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is mathematically standard and matches the joint-preservation leaf, but no cited source or inspectable locator supports the exact and adjacent-integer cardinality guarantees.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pairwise Independence Does Not Certify Negative Cylinders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between pairwise tests and all-subset product certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be uniform on \(\{000,011,101,110\}\). Its coordinates have marginal \(1/2\) and are pairwise independent, but \(\Pr(X_1=X_2=X_3=0)=1/4>1/8=\prod_i\Pr(X_i=0)\). Hence pairwise independence, and therefore pairwise nonpositive covariance alone, does not imply the all-subset negative-cylinder certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three even-parity bits pass all pairwise independence tests but violate the three-coordinate all-zero product bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Independence Does Not Certify Negative Cylinders

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Product Bounds Do Not Give Two-Sided Concentration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of separate selected and complementary cylinder inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\) uniform on \(\{000,011,101,110\}\), the selected-coordinate inequalities \(\mathbb E[\prod_{i\in S}X_i]\le\prod_{i\in S}\mathbb E[X_i]\) hold for every \(S\subseteq\{1,2,3\}\), while the complementary inequality fails for \(S=\{1,2,3\}\). Thus selected-coordinate bounds alone do not certify the complementary lower-tail side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All upper-cylinder inequalities may hold while the complementary all-zero inequality fails, so both certificate families are needed for two-sided conclusions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall S,\ \mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{i\in S}X_i\right]\le\prod_{i\in S}\mathbb E[X_i],\quad \mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{i=1}^3(1-X_i)\right]>\prod_{i=1}^3\mathbb E[1-X_i].
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Product Bounds Do Not Give Two-Sided Concentration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of the two-sided certificate under coordinate complementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) satisfies both negative-cylinder product inequalities with marginals \(x_i\), then \(Y_i=1-X_i\) satisfies the same two families with marginals \(1-x_i\); the selected-coordinate and unselected-coordinate inequalities exchange roles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementing every bit preserves the two-sided negative-cylinder certificate and swaps its two product-inequality families.
assumptions_latex: Both product inequalities hold for \(X\) on every coordinate subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y\text{ satisfies both product inequalities with marginals }1-x_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Complement Symmetry of Negative-Cylinder Certificates
Negative-Correlation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-moment certificates for both selected and unselected coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) have marginals \(\mathbb E[X_i]=x_i\). The two families of inequalities
\[\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{i\in S}X_i\right]\leq\prod_{i\in S}x_i,\qquad \mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{i\in S}(1-X_i)\right]\leq\prod_{i\in S}(1-x_i)\]
for every \(S\subseteq[n]\) certify negative cylinder dependence. Consequently, for any nonnegative coefficients \(a_i\), standard independent-variable Chernoff upper-tail bounds apply to \(\sum_i a_iX_i\), and the corresponding lower-tail bounds follow from the complementary inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Product-moment inequalities for selected and unselected coordinates certify the negative dependence needed to transfer standard Chernoff concentration bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\prod_{i\in S}X_i]\leq\prod_{i\in S}x_i\) and \(\mathbb E[\prod_{i\in S}(1-X_i)]\leq\prod_{i\in S}(1-x_i)\) for all \(S\subseteq[n]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf, but the product inequalities and their transfer to weighted Chernoff upper- and lower-tail bounds require an authoritative citation with a precise locator.
