knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why maximizing-endpoint pipage requires exchange convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(P=\{(t,1-t):0\leq t\leq1\}\), let \(F(x)=-(x_1-x_2)^2\). At \(x=(1/2,1/2)\), \(F(x)=0\), while both integral endpoints have value \(-1\). Thus selecting the better endpoint can decrease a maximization objective when the exchange restriction is concave.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Better-endpoint pipage can decrease a maximization objective when exchange convexity is reversed.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Curvature Orientation Boundary
Deterministic Polyhedral Pipage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint pipage over a polytope admitting pairwise feasible exchange directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a point \(x^0\) in a polytope \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) and an objective \(F:P\to\mathbb R\) convex on every feasible line parallel to \(e_i-e_j\). At iteration \(t\), if \(x^t\) is nonintegral, choose indices \(i\neq j\) and maximal \(\alpha,\beta>0\) such that \(x^t+z(e_i-e_j)\in P\) for \(z\in[-\beta,\alpha]\). Set \(x^{t+1}\) to the endpoint having larger \(F\)-value. Continue until an integral vertex is reached and output it. Each step satisfies \(F(x^{t+1})\geq F(x^t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move deterministically to the better endpoint of each feasible exchange segment; convexity preserves the objective until an integral vertex is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) is a polytope with terminating pairwise exchange steps
\(F\) is convex along every chosen exchange segment

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the class of polytopes for which pairwise endpoint steps always exist and terminate at an integral vertex is encoded only as an assumption and needs a precise source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating marginal preservation from negative dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=(0,\ldots,0)\) with probability \(1/2\) and \(X=(1,\ldots,1)\) with probability \(1/2\). Then \(\mathbb E[X_i]=1/2\) for every coordinate, but, for \(n>1\), \(\mathbb E[\prod_{i=1}^nX_i]=1/2>2^{-n}=\prod_i\mathbb E[X_i]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact coordinate marginals alone allow perfect positive correlation and do not imply Chernoff concentration.
assumptions_latex: The vector is all zero or all one with equal probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[X_i]=1/2\text{ for all }i\), but \(\mathbb E[\prod_iX_i]>\prod_i\mathbb E[X_i]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Marginals Do Not Imply Concentration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cylinder inequalities and concentration for standard matroid pipage rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let standard randomized pipage rounding on a matroid polytope, using a base extension when needed, start from \(x\) and terminate at \(X\in\{0,1\}^E\). Then, for every \(S\subseteq E\), \(\mathbb E[\prod_{e\in S}X_e]\leq\prod_{e\in S}x_e\) and \(\mathbb E[\prod_{e\in S}(1-X_e)]\leq\prod_{e\in S}(1-x_e)\). Consequently, nonnegative linear loads with coefficients in \([0,1]\) satisfy the corresponding independent-Bernoulli Chernoff upper- and lower-tail bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matroid pipage rounding supplies negative cylinder dependence, so bounded nonnegative linear loads have Chernoff concentration.
assumptions_latex: The domain is a matroid polytope and standard randomized pipage rounding is applied, with a valid base extension if necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\prod_{e\in S}X_e]\leq\prod_{e\in S}x_e\) and \(\mathbb E[\prod_{e\in S}(1-X_e)]\leq\prod_{e\in S}(1-x_e)\) for every \(S\subseteq E\).

notation.meaning: Rounded inclusion indicator for element e.
Bounded nonnegative coefficient in a rounded load.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Correlation Guarantee
Randomized Pipage Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation-preserving random endpoint selection on feasible exchange segments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x^0=x\in P\subseteq[0,1]^n\). At a nonintegral iterate \(x^t\), choose a feasible exchange direction \(d=e_i-e_j\) and maximal endpoints \(x^+=x^t+\alpha d\) and \(x^-=x^t-\beta d\), where \(\alpha,\beta>0\). Set \(x^{t+1}=x^+\) with probability \(\beta/(\alpha+\beta)\), and set \(x^{t+1}=x^-\) otherwise. Stop at an integral vertex \(X\). Then \(\mathbb E[x^{t+1}\mid x^t]=x^t\), hence \(\mathbb E[X]=x\). If \(F\) is convex along every chosen segment, then \(\mathbb E[F(X)]\geq F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random endpoint probabilities preserve the current fractional vector in expectation, yielding exact marginals and nondecreasing expected value for exchange-convex objectives.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex along chosen exchange segments when the value guarantee is invoked

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The martingale endpoint update is standard and the algorithm kind fits, but termination at an integral vertex and applicability to the stated polytope class need an authoritative source and locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exchange convexity without submodularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\{1,2\}\), define \(f(\{1,2\})=1\) and all other values as zero. Its multilinear extension is \(F(x)=x_1x_2\), and on \(x_1+x_2=1\), \(F(t,1-t)=t(1-t)\) is strictly concave.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive discrete complementarity can make the multilinear extension concave rather than convex along exchanges.
knowledge_statements.title: Non-Submodular Curvature Reversal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-difference identity characterizing exchange-line curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the multilinear extension \(F\) of \(f:2^{[n]}\to\mathbb R\) and distinct \(i,j\), \(\partial_{ij}^2F(x)=\mathbb E[f(R\cup\{i,j\})-f(R\cup\{i\})-f(R\cup\{j\})+f(R)]\), where \(R\subseteq[n]\setminus\{i,j\}\) is independently sampled according to the remaining coordinates. For \(g(z)=F(x+z(e_i-e_j))\), \(g''(z)=-2\partial_{ij}^2F\). Hence submodularity implies \(g''(z)\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixed derivative is the expected discrete second difference, and exchange-line curvature is its negative twice over.

notation.meaning: Mixed second partial derivative in coordinates i and j.
Independent random subset excluding i and j.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Hessian Representation
Multilinear-Extension Pipage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange convexity of the multilinear extension of a submodular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a submodular function \(f:2^{[n]}\to\mathbb R\), define its multilinear extension by
\[F(x)=\mathbb E[f(R_x)]=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}f(S)\prod_{i\in S}x_i\prod_{i\notin S}(1-x_i),\]
where elements enter \(R_x\) independently with probabilities \(x_i\). For distinct \(i,j\), the univariate map \(z\mapsto F(x+z(e_i-e_j))\) is convex on every interval contained in \([0,1]^n\). Therefore deterministic pipage can choose a feasible endpoint without decreasing \(F\), while randomized pipage preserves or increases its expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular function’s multilinear extension is convex along pairwise exchange lines, enabling deterministic or randomized pipage without loss in value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z\mapsto F(x+z(e_i-e_j))\) is convex for every \(i\neq j\).

notation.meaning: multilinear extension of the set function
independent random set with marginals x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exchange-line convexity statement and property kind fit this leaf, but no source is cited for the multilinear-extension formula and convexity conclusion.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of a Two-Base Merge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primitive exchange count, excluding exchange-pair search cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each update makes at least one additional element common to the two current bases and never removes an already common element. Therefore bases \(B_1,B_2\) of rank \(r\) merge after at most \(|B_1\setminus B_2|=|B_2\setminus B_1|\le r\) exchange iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-base merge finishes in at most the initial symmetric-difference half-size, and hence at most the rank.
assumptions_latex: \(B_1,B_2\) are bases of one rank-\(r\) matroid.
Every selected pair is a feasible symmetric exchange.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination of a Two-Base Merge

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative Cylinder Dependence of a Weighted Merge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence invariant of the primitive merge of two deterministic bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be the output of weighted swap rounding applied to \(B_1,B_2\) with weights \(a,b>0\), put \(y=(a\mathbf1_{B_1}+b\mathbf1_{B_2})/(a+b)\), and let \(X_e=\mathbf1\{e\in B\}\). For every \(S\subseteq E\), \[\mathbb E\prod_{e\in S}X_e\le\prod_{e\in S}y_e,\qquad \mathbb E\prod_{e\in S}(1-X_e)\le\prod_{e\in S}(1-y_e).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted two-base merge has upper and lower negative-cylinder dependence relative to its weighted input marginals.
assumptions_latex: \(B_1,B_2\) are bases of one finite matroid.
The prescribed weight-dependent symmetric-exchange updates are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output indicators satisfy both displayed cylinder inequalities.

notation.meaning: weighted average of the input incidence vectors

knowledge_statements.title: Negative Cylinder Dependence of a Weighted Merge
Matroid-Base Swap Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random symmetric exchanges merge two matroid bases while preserving weighted marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1,B_2\) be bases of a matroid and let \(a,b>0\). While \(B_1\neq B_2\), select \(i\in B_1\setminus B_2\) and \(j\in B_2\setminus B_1\) such that both \(B_1-i+j\) and \(B_2-j+i\) are bases. With probability \(a/(a+b)\), replace \(B_2\) by \(B_2-j+i\); otherwise replace \(B_1\) by \(B_1-i+j\). When the bases coincide, output their common base \(B\). The update preserves \(\mathbb E[(a+b)\mathbf1_B]=a\mathbf1_{B_1^{\rm in}}+b\mathbf1_{B_2^{\rm in}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated randomized symmetric exchanges merge two weighted matroid bases into one base while preserving their weighted incidence vector in expectation.
assumptions_latex: \(B_1,B_2\) are bases of the same finite matroid
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) is a base and \(\mathbb E[\mathbf1_B]=(a\mathbf1_{B_1^{\rm in}}+b\mathbf1_{B_2^{\rm in}})/(a+b)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted two-base merge is an appropriate algorithm for this leaf, but the symmetric-exchange step and marginal-preservation invariant lack cited support.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rounding-phase bound after a convex decomposition is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rank-\(r\) matroid and a decomposition containing \(m\) bases, each of the \(m-1\) two-base merges uses at most \(r\) symmetric exchanges. Hence the sequential rounding phase uses at most \((m-1)r\) exchanges, excluding decomposition computation and the cost of finding exchange pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential merging uses at most rank times the number of merges in primitive exchange iterations.
assumptions_latex: The input is a convex decomposition into \(m\) bases of a rank-\(r\) matroid.
Each primitive merge uses feasible symmetric exchanges.

notation.meaning: number of bases in the decomposition

knowledge_statements.title: Exchange-Step Bound for Sequential Merging

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence guarantee for the base returned from an explicit convex decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be produced by sequential swap rounding from \(x=\sum_r\lambda_r\mathbf1_{B_r}\), and let \(X_e=\mathbf1\{e\in C\}\). For every \(S\subseteq E\), \[\mathbb E\prod_{e\in S}X_e\le\prod_{e\in S}x_e,\qquad \mathbb E\prod_{e\in S}(1-X_e)\le\prod_{e\in S}(1-x_e).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex-decomposition swap rounding preserves the input marginals and satisfies upper and lower negative-cylinder inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is supplied as a convex combination of bases of one finite matroid.
The bases are combined by sequential weighted swap merges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output indicators satisfy both negative-cylinder inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative Cylinder Dependence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected-objective guarantee for swap rounding an explicit base decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\) be submodular and let \(F(y)=\mathbb E[f(R_y)]\) be its multilinear extension. If \(C\) is obtained by convex-decomposition swap rounding of \(x\), then \(\mathbb E[f(C)]\ge F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Swap rounding does not decrease the multilinear-extension benchmark of a submodular objective in expectation.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is supplied as a convex combination of matroid bases.
\(C\) is produced by sequential swap rounding.

notation.meaning: independent random set with marginals y

knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Multilinear-Extension Guarantee
Convex-Decomposition Swap Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential merging of a convex decomposition into one random matroid base.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a matroid-base-polytope point \(x=\sum_{r=1}^m\lambda_r\mathbf1_{B_r}\), where each \(B_r\) is a base, \(\lambda_r>0\), and \(\sum_r\lambda_r=1\). Initialize \(C=B_1\) and \(s=\lambda_1\). For \(r=2,\ldots,m\), apply weighted matroid-base swap rounding to \(C,B_r\) with weights \(s,\lambda_r\), replace \(C\) by the resulting base, and set \(s\leftarrow s+\lambda_r\). Output \(C\). The final incidence vector satisfies \(\mathbb E[\mathbf1_C]=x\), so all element marginals equal the coordinates of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequentially merge the bases in a convex decomposition; the final random base preserves the original fractional point as its expected incidence vector.
assumptions_latex: \(x=\sum_{r=1}^m\lambda_r\mathbf1_{B_r}\) is a convex decomposition into bases
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is a matroid base and \(\mathbb E[\mathbf1_C]=x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequential convex-decomposition merge is correctly classified as an algorithm, but its expectation invariant and final marginal guarantee have no authoritative citation.

children.title: Maximum-Coverage Rounding
children.top_down_role: Correlation-aware rounding for selecting sets under coverage objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Coverage Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-correlation rounding of the standard budgeted maximum-coverage relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) be a finite universe with weights \(w_u\geq0\), let \(A_1,\ldots,A_n\subseteq U\), let \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), and let \(x\in[0,1]^n\) satisfy \(\sum_i x_i\leq k\). Apply cardinality-preserving dependent rounding to obtain \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\), and output the sets with \(X_i=1\). If the complementary negative-correlation inequalities hold, then every \(u\in U\) satisfies
\[\Pr\{u\text{ is covered}\}\geq1-\prod_{i:u\in A_i}(1-x_i)\geq(1-e^{-1})\min\!\left\{1,\sum_{i:u\in A_i}x_i\right\}.\]
Consequently, at most \(k\) sets are selected and the expected covered weight is at least \((1-1/e)\) times the projected coverage-relaxation value \(\sum_{u\in U}w_u\min\{1,\sum_{i:u\in A_i}x_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent rounding selects at most k sets and, under complementary negative correlation, covers each element with probability at least 1 minus the product of one minus x_i over sets containing that element, yielding the standard expected 1−1/e coverage guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) and the set family are finite
the rounding preserves the required cardinality bound and satisfies complementary negative correlation
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_iX_i\leq k\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[\sum_{u\text{ covered}}w_u]\geq(1-1/e)\sum_{u\in U}w_u\min\{1,\sum_{i:u\in A_i}x_i\}\).

notation.meaning: indicator that set i is selected

children.title: Submodular-Selection Rounding
children.top_down_role: Correlation-aware rounding for constrained selection under submodular objectives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates exchange rounding on a fixed base polytope from preliminary coordinatewise augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Submodularity makes the multilinear extension convex along matroid exchange directions and supports lossless endpoint rounding on a fixed base polytope. However, replacing x\in P(M) by y\in B(M) with y\ge x preserves value only for coordinatewise nondecreasing F. For the nonmonotone submodular function f(S)=-|S|, F(y)<F(x) whenever y>x in total coordinate sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Submodularity supports exchange rounding on a base, but monotonicity is essential when augmenting an independent-set point to a base point.
assumptions_latex: f is submodular with multilinear extension F

notation.meaning: fractional matroid points before and after augmentation

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity Boundary for Base Augmentation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extension from the Independence Polytope to a Base Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of monotone submodular rounding over independent sets to base rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P(M) be a finite matroid independence polytope and x\in P(M). There exists y\in B(M) with y\ge x coordinatewise. If f is monotone submodular with multilinear extension F, then F(y)\ge F(x). Applying marginal-preserving randomized pipage or swap rounding to y returns a random base B satisfying \mathbb E[f(B)]\ge F(y)\ge F(x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional independent-set point can be dominated by a base point, so monotonicity reduces independence-polytope rounding to base rounding without expected-value loss.
assumptions_latex: The base-rounding procedure preserves marginals and does not decrease expected multilinear value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists y\in B(M):y\ge x,\qquad \mathbb E[f(B)]\ge F(y)\ge F(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Extension from the Independence Polytope to a Base Polytope
Submodular-Selection Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Swap or pipage rounding for monotone submodular selection under a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R_{\geq0}\) be monotone submodular with multilinear extension \(F\), and let \(x\) lie in a matroid base polytope. Starting from either \(x\) or a convex decomposition of \(x\) into bases, apply randomized pipage rounding or convex-decomposition swap rounding and output the terminal base \(B\). Exchange-line convexity of \(F\) gives
\[\mathbb E[f(B)]=\mathbb E[F(\mathbf1_B)]\geq F(x),\]
while marginal preservation gives \(\Pr(e\in B)=x_e\) for every \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pipage or swap rounding converts a fractional matroid base into a random base without reducing expected multilinear-extension value or changing marginals.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) lies in a matroid base polytope
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) is a base, \(\mathbb E[f(B)]\geq F(x)\), and \(\Pr(e\in B)=x_e\) for all \(e\in E\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and local scope are appropriate, but the lossless expected-value guarantee for both pipage and swap rounding requires a precise authoritative citation.

children.title: Coverage-to-Submodularity Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Transfer of coverage-oriented rounding principles to broader submodular objectives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient and mixed-partial formulas for the multilinear extension of weighted coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For F(x)=\sum_{u\in U}w_u(1-\prod_{i:u\in A_i}(1-x_i)),  rac{\partial F}{\partial x_i}=\sum_{u\in A_i}w_u\prod_{j
e i:u\in A_j}(1-x_j)\ge0, and for i
e j,  rac{\partial^2F}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}=-\sum_{u\in A_i\cap A_j}w_u\prod_{\ell
otin\{i,j\}:u\in A_\ell}(1-x_\ell)\le0. Nonnegative weights are essential: if one element has weight -1 and belongs to both A_1 and A_2, the resulting set function is neither monotone nor submodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coverage extensions have nonnegative first derivatives and nonpositive mixed derivatives; signed weights can destroy both properties.

notation.meaning: set covered by selectable item i

knowledge_statements.title: Differential Structure of Coverage Extensions
Coverage-to-Submodularity Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted coverage as a monotone submodular function with an explicit multilinear extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For selectable sets \((A_i)_{i\in E}\) over a universe \(U\) with weights \(w_u\geq0\), define
\[f(S)=\sum_{u\in\bigcup_{i\in S}A_i}w_u.\]
Then \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R_{\geq0}\) is monotone and submodular. Its multilinear extension has the explicit form
\[F(x)=\sum_{u\in U}w_u\left(1-\prod_{i:u\in A_i}(1-x_i)\right),\qquad x\in[0,1]^E.\]
Hence any rounding guarantee formulated for monotone submodular multilinear extensions applies directly to weighted coverage after substituting this representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted coverage is monotone submodular, and its multilinear extension equals the sum of each element’s weight times its independent coverage probability.
assumptions_latex: \((A_i)_{i\in E}\) is a finite set system
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is monotone submodular and \(F(x)=\sum_{u\in U}w_u(1-\prod_{i:u\in A_i}(1-x_i))\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically standard and fits the interface leaf, but the record supplies no source or locator for submodularity and the explicit multilinear-extension formula.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary for general monotone submodular selection under one matroid constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(|S|\leq k\) is a uniform-matroid constraint and maximum coverage is a normalized monotone submodular special case, a polynomial-time \((1-1/e+\delta)\)-approximation for every explicitly represented instance under one matroid, for fixed \(\delta>0\), would exceed the maximum-coverage hardness threshold. Unless \(P=NP\), the general factor cannot be improved beyond \(1-1/e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform matroids already contain the maximum-coverage hardness barrier, making the continuous-greedy factor sharp in the general explicit-input model.
assumptions_latex: The model includes explicitly represented maximum-coverage instances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{No polynomial-time }(1-1/e+\delta)\text{-approximation exists for the general problem unless }P=NP.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Approximation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fractional domain used by pipage and swap rounding for independent-set selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) with rank function \(r\), \(P(M)=\{x\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^E:x(A)\leq r(A)\text{ for all }A\subseteq E\}=\operatorname{conv}\{\mathbf1_I:I\in\mathcal I\}\). Its full-rank face \(B(M)=\{x\in P(M):x(E)=r(E)\}\) is the convex hull of base-incidence vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rank-inequality polytope represents fractional independent-set selections, and its full-rank face represents bases.
assumptions_latex: \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) is a finite matroid with rank function \(r\).
knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Selection Polytope
Matroid-Constrained Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-greedy fractional selection followed by lossless matroid rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a matroid and let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R_{\geq0}\) be monotone submodular with \(f(\varnothing)=0\), accessed by a value oracle. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), continuous greedy computes a point \(x\) in the matroid polytope with
\[F(x)\geq(1-1/e-\varepsilon)\max_{S\in\mathcal I}f(S).\]
After extending \(x\) to an appropriate base-polytope point if necessary, pipage or swap rounding returns an independent set \(S\in\mathcal I\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[f(S)]\geq F(x)\). Thus the combined randomized algorithm is a \((1-1/e-\varepsilon)\)-approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous greedy plus pipage or swap rounding gives a randomized 1−1/e−ε approximation for monotone submodular maximization under a matroid constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid with an independence oracle
\(f\) is nonnegative, monotone, submodular, and normalized

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the selection leaf, but the oracle-model approximation guarantee, computation of the fractional point, and extension to a base-polytope instance require a precise theorem citation.

children.title: Scheduling Constraints
children.top_down_role: Correlation-aware rounding under assignment, timing, precedence, or resource restrictions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exact machine-load preservation for the assignment relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For three unit-size jobs and two identical machines, take \(T=3/2\) and \(x_{ij}=1/2\). Each fractional machine load is \(3/2\), but every integral assignment places at least two jobs on one machine and has makespan at least \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible assignment relaxation can require an additive machine-load increase after integral rounding.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Makespan Rounding Gap
Scheduling Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-load rounding for the unrelated-machines assignment relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{ij}\geq0\) be a fractional assignment of jobs \(j\) to machines \(i\), with processing times \(p_{ij}\geq0\), such that
\[\sum_i x_{ij}=1\quad\text{for every }j,\qquad \sum_jp_{ij}x_{ij}\leq T\quad\text{for every }i,\]
and \(x_{ij}=0\) whenever \(p_{ij}>T\). Assignment-polytope rounding yields an integral assignment \(\sigma\) for which every job is assigned exactly once and
\[\sum_{j:\sigma(j)=i}p_{ij}\leq T+\max_{j:\sigma(j)=i}p_{ij}\leq2T\]
for every machine \(i\). Thus exact assignment constraints survive rounding with at most one-job additive load violation per machine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible unrelated-machines LP assignment can be rounded exactly by job while increasing each machine’s load by at most one assigned job size.

notation.meaning: fractional assignment of job j to machine i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the scheduling-constraints leaf, but the one-job additive load bound for unrelated-machine assignment rounding requires an authoritative theorem and exact locator.

children.title: Routing Constraints
children.top_down_role: Correlation-aware rounding under path, flow, connectivity, or congestion restrictions.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a directed network with capacities \(u_e\ge 0\).
Each commodity \(i\) has demand \(d_i\ge 0\), terminals \((s_i,t_i)\), and an admissible path family \(\mathcal P_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i d_i\sum_{P\in\mathcal P_i:e\in P}X_{iP}\le u_e\) for every \(e\in E\).

notation.meaning: Fractional weight assigned to path P for commodity i.
Indicator that commodity i is routed on path P.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsplittable path-routing feasibility; probabilistic congestion bounds require a separate rounding theorem.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.3 Multicommodity Flow Problems p. 17
source_refs.source_title: Network Optimization: Continuous and Discrete Models

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fractional path assignment satisfies \(x_{iP}\ge 0\), \(\sum_{P\in\mathcal P_i}x_{iP}=1\) for every commodity \(i\), and \(\sum_i d_i\sum_{P\in\mathcal P_i:e\in P}x_{iP}\le u_e\) for every edge \(e\). An integral routing is represented by \(X_{iP}\in\{0,1\}\) with \(\sum_{P\in\mathcal P_i}X_{iP}=1\). Exact routing constraints require the displayed capacity inequalities with \(x_{iP}\) replaced by \(X_{iP}\); an approximation may instead certify a stated multiplicative or additive congestion relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Routing constraints select one admissible path per commodity and require every edge's total routed demand to respect its capacity, possibly with an explicitly stated congestion relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Routing Constraints

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.3 Multicommodity Flow Problems p. 17
source_witnesses.source_title: Network Optimization: Continuous and Discrete Models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between fractional path feasibility and exact unsplittable feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let three unit-demand commodities each choose between two common parallel resources of capacity \(3/2\). Assign every commodity fraction \(1/2\) to each resource. Both fractional loads are \(3/2\), but every integral choice puts at least two commodities on one resource and creates load \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible fractional routing can lack any exactly capacity-feasible unsplittable rounding.
assumptions_latex: Each commodity may use either of two common resources.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Every integral routing has maximum resource load at least }2>3/2.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Capacity Rounding Gap

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-edge concentration for independently rounded fractional path assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Independently choose for each commodity \(i\) a path according to \(x_{iP}\). For edge \(e\), let \(L_e=\sum_i d_i\mathbf1[e\in P_i]\), \(p_{ie}=\sum_{P\ni e}x_{iP}\), \(\mu_e=\sum_i d_ip_{ie}\leq u_e\), \(b_e=\max\{d_i:p_{ie}>0\}\), and \(\sigma_e^2=\sum_i d_i^2p_{ie}(1-p_{ie})\). Then, for \(t\geq0\), \(\Pr[L_e>u_e+t]\leq\exp[-t^2/(2(\sigma_e^2+b_et/3))]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent path rounding preserves each commodity's path distribution and gives Bernstein-type congestion tails, but does not ensure exact capacities.

notation.meaning: Fractional probability that commodity i uses edge e.
Largest demand with positive probability of using edge e.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Path-Rounding Congestion Bound

children.title: Degree Constraints
children.top_down_role: Correlation-aware rounding under local incidence or degree bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cycle-and-path implementation of bipartite degree-dependent rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Repeatedly choose an even cycle or a maximal path in the fractional support and alternately increase and decrease its edge values to the two maximal feasible endpoints. Choose between those endpoints with probabilities preserving the conditional mean. Internal incident sums are unchanged, path-endpoint sums remain within their initial floor-ceiling intervals, and at least one fractional edge becomes integral at each update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating endpoint updates on fractional support cycles and paths integralize edges while preserving marginals and controlling degrees.
assumptions_latex: The fractional support graph is bipartite.
Only currently fractional support edges are updated.
Endpoint probabilities preserve the current vector conditionally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\{0,1\}^E\) is obtained after at most \(|E|\) updates and has the marginal and floor-ceiling degree guarantees.

notation.meaning: Edge set of the bipartite support graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternating Support Rounding

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Odd-Cycle Obstruction to Simultaneous Degree Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of universal floor-ceiling degree preservation outside suitable incidence structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(C_3\), set \(x_e=1/2\) for every edge. Then \(d_x(v)=1\) at every vertex, while no \(X\in\{0,1\}^{E(C_3)}\) has \(d_X(v)=1\) at all three vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Half-weighting a triangle gives integral fractional degrees that no integral edge set can preserve simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Cycle Obstruction to Simultaneous Degree Rounding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard sufficient incidence structure for simultaneous floor-ceiling degree preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(U\cup W,E)\) be bipartite and \(x\in[0,1]^E\). Bipartite dependent rounding produces \(X\in\{0,1\}^E\) such that \(\mathbb E[X_e]=x_e\) for every \(e\), \(d_X(v)\in\{\lfloor d_x(v)\rfloor,\lceil d_x(v)\rceil\}\) for every \(v\), and, for every \(v\) and \(S\subseteq\delta(v)\), \(\mathbb E[\prod_{e\in S}X_e]\leq\prod_{e\in S}x_e\) and \(\mathbb E[\prod_{e\in S}(1-X_e)]\leq\prod_{e\in S}(1-x_e)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bipartite dependent rounding preserves edge marginals, rounds every vertex degree to its floor or ceiling, and gives local negative cylinder dependence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[X_e]=x_e\) and \(\lfloor d_x(v)\rfloor\leq d_X(v)\leq\lceil d_x(v)\rceil\), with the stated cylinder inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Bipartite Dependent-Rounding Degree Guarantee

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lfloor d_x(v)\rfloor\le d_X(v)\le\lceil d_x(v)\rceil\) for every constrained vertex \(v\).

notation.meaning: Rounded integral degree of vertex v.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-one degree preservation as a rounding target, not a universal guarantee for arbitrary edge polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a specified vertex set \(W\subseteq V\), the additive-one degree constraint requires each rounded incidence vector \(X\) to satisfy \(\lfloor d_x(v)\rfloor\le d_X(v)\le\lceil d_x(v)\rceil\) for every \(v\in W\). If \(d_x(v)\) is integral, this reduces to \(d_X(v)=d_x(v)\). Marginal preservation is the separate requirement \(\mathbb E[X_e]=x_e\) for every \(e\in E\); neither condition alone implies that all degree bounds can be imposed simultaneously without additional polyhedral structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degree-aware rounding targets an integral degree within the floor and ceiling of each fractional degree; exact preservation follows when that fractional degree is integral.
knowledge_statements.title: Degree Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The floor-ceiling degree target is precise and correctly qualified as nonuniversal, but no source supports the required polyhedral conditions or identifies a rounding family that attains the simultaneous bounds.

children.title: Cross-Domain Transfer
children.top_down_role: Shared preservation principles spanning scheduling, routing, plus degree-bounded settings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise-exchange accessibility is independent of polyhedral integrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The integral polytope \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,1)\}\subseteq[0,1]^2\) contains \(x=(1/2,1/2)\), but \(\{x+t(e_1-e_2):t\in\mathbb R\}\cap P=\{x\}\). Thus integrality alone does not ensure a feasible pipage exchange from every fractional point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integral polytope can contain a fractional point with no feasible pairwise pipage move.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ is integral, but no nonzero }e_1-e_2\text{ displacement is feasible at }x.\)

notation.meaning: Fractional point without a feasible pairwise exchange.

knowledge_statements.title: Integral-Polytope Exchange Boundary
Cross-Domain Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract transfer principle for pipage-style maximization with convex restrictions along feasible swap directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in P\). Suppose each nonintegral iterate admits distinct coordinates \(i,j\) and a nondegenerate feasible segment \(\{x+t(e_i-e_j):t\in[a,b]\}\subseteq P\) whose selected endpoint reduces the number of fractional coordinates. If the restriction of \(F\) to every such segment is convex, deterministic selection of an endpoint maximizing \(F\) yields a terminal integral point \(X\) satisfying \(F(X)\ge F(x)\). Alternatively, choosing the two endpoints with probabilities that preserve their conditional mean yields \(\mathbb E[X]=x\) and \(\mathbb E[F(X)]\ge F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pipage-style maximization transfers to a domain whose feasible region supports terminating pairwise swaps and whose objective is convex along every swap segment. Greedy endpoints preserve the objective deterministically, while mean-preserving randomized endpoints preserve marginals and the objective in expectation.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) is preserved by the permitted pairwise swap directions, and the endpoint process terminates at an integral point.
\(F:[0,1]^n\to\mathbb R\) is convex on every feasible swap segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deterministic maximizing endpoint choices give \(F(X)\ge F(x)\); mean-preserving randomized choices give \(\mathbb E[X]=x\) and \(\mathbb E[F(X)]\ge F(x)\).

notation.meaning: Objective or potential extended to fractional points.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional-expectation derandomization of k-median facility rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A k-median specialization of the method of conditional expectation that fixes the initial facility set and residual facilities without increasing expected cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: First compute the expected cost conditional on opening A and the expected cost conditional on opening B', and choose the option having smaller expectation. Initialize D=\varnothing. While |D|<k-k_1, choose i\in B\setminus(B'\cup D) for which the conditional expected cost after replacing D by D\cup\{i\} is no greater than the current conditional expectation, and then add i to D. Such an i exists because the current conditional expectation is the average of the conditional expectations obtained by fixing each eligible next facility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose whichever of A and B' gives the smaller conditional expected cost. Then fix the remaining facilities one at a time, always choosing a facility whose conditional expected completion cost does not exceed the current expectation. The averaging identity guarantees that an eligible choice exists at each step.
assumptions_latex: \text{The required conditional expectations are efficiently computable}

source_evidence.locator: k-Median / 25.3. Randomized rounding / Algorithm 25.3-extra-2

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost of explicit sequential branch minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Z_i\) has finite domain \(D_i\), and evaluating one stage-\(i\) conditional expectation costs at most \(T_i\). Testing every branch uses at most \(\sum_{i=1}^m|D_i|\) evaluations and time \(O(\sum_{i=1}^m|D_i|T_i)\), apart from selection overhead. The method is polynomial-time when this total is polynomial, or when an equivalent efficient conditional-minimization oracle is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit conditional-expectation fixing tests the branches of each variable; efficiency requires polynomial total branch-evaluation cost or an efficient minimization oracle.
assumptions_latex: T_i\text{ bounds one stage-i conditional-expectation evaluation}

notation.meaning: Domain of the ith random choice.
Cost of one stage-i conditional-expectation evaluation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Payoff-maximization form of sequential conditional fixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m)\) be an integrable payoff on a finite sequential experiment. If each stage fixes the next variable to a value maximizing the resulting conditional expectation, the completed assignment \(z\) satisfies \(R(z)\ge\mathbb E[R(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing a branch of maximum conditional expected payoff yields a deterministic outcome at least as good as the original expected payoff.
assumptions_latex: Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\text{ generate a finite sequential probability space}
\text{Required conditional expectations can be evaluated or maximized}
knowledge_statements.title: Maximization Form of Conditional Expectations

assumptions_latex: The objective \(C(Z_1,,,Z_m)\) and required conditional expectations are computable.

notation.meaning: Conditional expected cost after fixing a prefix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential deterministic derandomization for a finite-valued minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with no variables fixed and \(M_0=\mathbb E[C(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m)]\). At stage \(i\), for every value \(a\) in the support of \(Z_i\), compute \(M_i(a)=\mathbb E[C(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m)\mid Z_1=z_1,\ldots,Z_{i-1}=z_{i-1},Z_i=a]\). Choose a value \(z_i\) minimizing \(M_i(a)\). Since the current conditional expectation is a convex combination of these branch values, the chosen value does not increase it. After stage \(m\), output \(z=(z_1,,,z_m)\), whose deterministic cost is at most \(M_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix random choices sequentially, always selecting a branch with no larger conditional expected cost; the final deterministic solution matches or improves the original expectation.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Expectation Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-expectation algorithm and minimization guarantee are standard, but no source is supplied. The occurrences of triple commas corrupt tuple notation, and the convex-combination explanation is proof text rather than a knowledge statement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous-avoidance certificate for several bad events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_r\) be bad events and let \(\Phi_j(\sigma)\ge\Pr(B_j\mid\sigma)\) be nonnegative estimators. Set \(\Phi(\sigma)=\sum_{j=1}^r\Phi_j(\sigma)\). If every reachable partial assignment has a supported branch with \(\Phi(\sigma,a)\le\Phi(\sigma)\), then \(\Phi(\varnothing)<1\) certifies that greedy nonincreasing branch selection produces a complete assignment outside \(\bigcup_{j=1}^rB_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum of event estimators certifies simultaneous avoidance when the sum starts below one and always has a nonincreasing branch.
assumptions_latex: \text{Every reachable partial assignment has a supported nonincreasing branch}

notation.meaning: Estimator for the jth bad event.

review_flags: nonincrease of the sum is an explicit assumption; it does not follow from separate estimators alone
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Pessimistic Estimator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local condition guaranteeing a nonincreasing estimator branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partial assignment \(\sigma\), suppose the next random choice takes values \(a\) with conditional probabilities \(p_a\). If \[\sum_a p_a\Phi(\sigma,a)\le\Phi(\sigma),\] then some value with \(p_a>0\) satisfies \(\Phi(\sigma,a)\le\Phi(\sigma)\). The conditional-average inequality is therefore sufficient for greedy estimator descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the probability-weighted average child estimator does not exceed the parent, some supported child is nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Average Sufficient Condition

assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a bad event in a finite sequential random experiment.
A nonnegative estimator \(\Phi\) is computable on every reachable partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\Phi(\varnothing)<1\), greedy branch selection produces a complete assignment outside \(B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic avoidance certificate based on a recursively nonincreasing upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pessimistic estimator for \(B\) is a function \(\Phi\) such that \(\Pr(B\mid\sigma)\le\Phi(\sigma)\) for every reachable partial assignment \(\sigma\), and whenever the next variable has admissible values \(a\), some branch satisfies \(\Phi(\sigma,a)\le\Phi(\sigma)\). For every complete assignment \(z\in B\), require \(\Phi(z)\ge 1\). Beginning at the empty assignment, repeatedly choose a nonincreasing branch. If \(\Phi(\varnothing)<1\), the terminal assignment has estimator below one and therefore cannot belong to \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pessimistic estimator upper-bounds failure and always has a nonincreasing branch; starting below one certifies that greedy fixing avoids the bad event.
knowledge_statements.title: Pessimistic Estimators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate conditions are mathematically coherent, but they lack a direct source. The final inference is presented as proof text and should be replaced by a concise certificate guarantee after sourcing.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of limited independence to control a global event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be uniform on \(\{y\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i y_i\equiv0\pmod2\}\), where \(n\ge2\). Every subfamily of at most \(n-1\) coordinates is uniform and independent, but \(\Pr[\sum_iY_i\equiv0\pmod2]=1\); fully independent unbiased bits give probability \(1/2\). Thus \((n-1)\)-wise independence need not reproduce events depending on all \(n\) coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform even-parity bits are independent on every proper subfamily but completely determine global parity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y\text{ is }(n-1)\text{-wise independent but not }n\text{-wise independent}
knowledge_statements.title: Parity Boundary for Limited Independence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional definition for a finite family of discrete random variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Discrete random variables \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) are \(k\)-wise independent if, for every \(I\subseteq[n]\) with \(|I|\le k\), the joint law of \((Y_i)_{i\in I}\) equals the product of its marginal laws. Equivalently, for all values \((a_i)_{i\in I}\), \[\Pr[\forall i\in I:\,Y_i=a_i]=\prod_{i\in I}\Pr[Y_i=a_i].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family is k-wise independent when every subfamily of at most k variables is jointly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall I\subseteq[n],\ |I|\le k:\quad \mathcal L((Y_i)_{i\in I})=\bigotimes_{i\in I}\mathcal L(Y_i)
knowledge_statements.title: k-Wise Independence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multilinear statistics determined by k-wise independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) be \(k\)-wise independent. Every multilinear polynomial \(P(Y)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n],\,|S|\le k}c_S\prod_{i\in S}Y_i\) of degree at most \(k\) satisfies \[\mathbb E[P(Y)]=\sum_{|S|\le k}c_S\prod_{i\in S}\mathbb E[Y_i],\] the same value obtained from fully independent variables with the same marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: k-wise independence reproduces expectations of multilinear statistics involving at most k coordinates.
assumptions_latex: Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\text{ are k-wise independent and integrable}
P\text{ is multilinear of degree at most }k

Evaluation at the ith field point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial-evaluation construction of uniform finite-field variables with bounded independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sample independent uniform coefficients \(c_0,,,c_{k-1}\in\mathbb F_q\) and form \(p(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}c_jt^j\). Output \(Y_i=p(a_i)\) for \(i=1,,,n\). For any \(r\le k\) distinct indices, evaluation at their points is a surjective linear map from \(\mathbb F_q^k\) to \(\mathbb F_q^r\), so those \(r\) outputs are jointly uniform. Enumerating all \(q^k\) coefficient vectors yields an explicit sample space supporting the same \(k\)-wise independent distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate a random degree-below-k polynomial at distinct field points; any k outputs are jointly uniform, and all coefficient vectors explicitly enumerate the sample space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility guarantee obtained by exhaustive finite-support search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\subseteq\Omega\) be the acceptable points in a finite supported distribution. If \(\Pr_{\omega\sim w}[\omega\in G]>0\), exhaustive enumeration of \(\Omega\) with a deterministic membership test returns an acceptable point. Equivalently, if a bad event has probability below one, some support point avoids it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive success probability certifies that exhaustive search of the finite support finds a successful outcome.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary for full structured-support search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_n\) be explicitly enumerable, and suppose generating and evaluating one point costs at most \(T(n)\). Full enumeration takes \(O(|\Omega_n|T(n))\) time plus bookkeeping. Consequently, the direct method is polynomial-time when \(|\Omega_n|T(n)=n^{O(1)}\); a succinct description alone does not make full search polynomial when the support is exponential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full structured enumeration is polynomial only when support size and per-point work have polynomial total cost.

notation.meaning: Structured sample space for instances of size n.
Per-point generation and evaluation upper bound.

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) is a finite explicitly enumerable sample space with distribution weights \(w_\omega\ge 0\).
The objective \(C(\omega)\) is deterministically evaluable for every \(\omega\in\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive deterministic search over a compact explicit sample space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Enumerate every \(\omega\in\Omega\), evaluate \(C(\omega)\), and retain a point \(\widehat\omega\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\omegaiction\Omega}C(\omega)\). Because \(\sum_{\omegaestrictions\Omega}w_\omega=1\), the minimum is at most the weighted average: \(C(\widehat\omega)\le\sum_{\omegaestrictions\Omega}w_\omega C(\omega)=\mathbb E[C]\). Thus any performance guarantee expressed as an upper bound on the randomized construction's expected cost is inherited by the selected point. The running time is \(O(|\Omega|T_C)\), where \(T_C\) bounds one evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate a compact explicit sample space and return its best point; its cost cannot exceed the distribution's average cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rowwise and simultaneous feasibility guarantee for independently rounded binary covering systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}, independently let X_j\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_j), and put \mu_i=\sum_jA_{ij}q_j. For 0<\delta<1, \Pr[(AX)_i<(1-\delta)\mu_i]\le e^{-\delta^2\mu_i/2}. If (1-\delta)\mu_i\ge b_i for every i, then \Pr[AX\not\ge b]\le\sum_i e^{-\delta^2\mu_i/2}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent rounding covers every row with positive or high probability when each row has sufficient expected coverage and slack.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Rounding Coverage Bound

assumptions_latex: \(U\) is a finite ground set and \(\mathcal S\subseteq2^U\) is a family of selectable sets.
Each element \(e\in U\) has a required multiplicity \(b_e\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility is equivalent to \(Ax\ge b\) with \(x\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal S}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A covering system selects a subfamily encoded by \(x\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal S}\) such that every element receives its required coverage: \(\sum_{S\in\mathcal S:e\in S}x_S\ge b_e\) for all \(e\in U\), equivalently \(Ax\ge b\). With nonnegative costs \(c_S\), the optimization problem minimizes \(\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}c_Sx_S\). Replacing the binary domain by \(0\le x_S\le1\) gives the standard fractional relaxation from which a rounding algorithm constructs a covering subfamily.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A covering system chooses sets so that every ground element is contained in at least its required number of chosen sets.

children.title: Packing Systems
children.top_down_role: Randomized-rounding problem families governed by resource or upper-bound requirements.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rowwise and simultaneous overload guarantee for independently rounded binary packing systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}, independently let X_j\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_j), and put \mu_i=\sum_jA_{ij}q_j. For \delta>0, \Pr[(AX)_i>(1+\delta)\mu_i]\le\left(e^\delta/(1+\delta)^{1+\delta}\right)^{\mu_i}. Consequently, if (1+\delta_i)\mu_i\le b_i for every i, then \Pr[AX\not\le b]\le\sum_i\left(e^{\delta_i}/(1+\delta_i)^{1+\delta_i}\right)^{\mu_i}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent rounding has a Chernoff upper-tail bound for each packing row, and a union bound controls all overloads.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A packing system selects a subfamily encoded by \(x\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal S}\) without exceeding any resource capacity: \(\sum_{S\in\mathcal S:e\in S}x_S\le b_e\) for all \(e\in U\), equivalently \(Ax\le b\). With nonnegative profits \(p_S\), the optimization problem maximizes \(\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}p_Sx_S\). Replacing the binary domain by \(0\le x_S\le1\) gives the standard fractional relaxation from which a rounding algorithm constructs a feasible or explicitly capacity-relaxed packing.

children.title: Set-System Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding organized by incidence structure, frequency, discrepancy, or set interactions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective accounting for deletion and addition repairs after set-system rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Y_S\in\{0,1\} be initial indicators and X_S\in\{0,1\} altered indicators. For nonnegative profits w_S, if X_S\le Y_S and \Pr[X_S=1\mid Y_S=1]\ge\rho_S, then \mathbb E[\sum_Sw_SX_S]\ge\sum_Sw_S\rho_S\Pr[Y_S=1]. For nonnegative costs c_S, if X_S\ge Y_S and \Pr[X_S=1]\le\Pr[Y_S=1]+a_S, then \mathbb E[\sum_Sc_SX_S]\le\sum_Sc_S(\Pr[Y_S=1]+a_S).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deletion repairs are controlled by survival probabilities, while addition repairs are controlled by added-selection probabilities.
assumptions_latex: The stated deletion or addition coupling holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[w^TX]\ge\sum_Sw_S\rho_S\Pr[Y_S=1]\text{ for deletions, with the displayed cost bound for additions}.

notation.meaning: Upper bound on the added selection probability.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pairwise Dependent Rounding for a Cardinality Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependent rounding of fractional set-selection variables having integral total.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in[0,1]^m\) and suppose \(r=\sum_{i=1}^m x_i\in\mathbb Z\). While two coordinates \(x_i,x_j\) are fractional, set
\[\alpha=\min\{1-x_i,x_j\},\qquad \beta=\min\{x_i,1-x_j\}.\]
Replace \((x_i,x_j)\) by \((x_i+\alpha,x_j-\alpha)\) with probability \(\beta/(\alpha+\beta)\), and by \((x_i-\beta,x_j+\beta)\) otherwise. The procedure terminates with \(X\in\{0,1\}^m\), preserves \(\sum_iX_i=r\) surely, and satisfies \(\mathbb E[X_i]=x_i\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly move a fractional pair to one of two boundary points while preserving its sum and each coordinate's expectation.

notation.meaning: Maximum feasible pairwise moves in the two directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Dependent Rounding for a Cardinality Polytope

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration and implementation bound for the cardinality-preserving variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each pairwise update makes at least one selected fractional coordinate integral and never makes an integral coordinate fractional. Because an integral total precludes exactly one remaining fractional coordinate, the procedure uses at most \(m-1\) updates and can be implemented in \(O(m)\) arithmetic operations by maintaining a list of fractional coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pairwise dependent-rounding procedure terminates after linearly many boundary moves.
assumptions_latex: The pairwise dependent-rounding algorithm above is used.
Fractional coordinates are maintained in a mutable list.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{At most }m-1\text{ updates and }O(m)\text{ arithmetic operations are required}.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Dependent-Rounding Termination Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small incidence system showing that cardinality-rounding invariants do not imply unrelated feasibility constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(1/2,1/2)\) and apply exact-cardinality dependent rounding, so \(X_1+X_2=1\) surely and \(\mathbb E[X_i]=1/2\). The additional incidence condition \(X_1=X_2\) is nevertheless violated surely. Thus preserved marginals and total cardinality alone do not imply feasibility for an arbitrary additional incidence system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact total and correct marginals can still violate an additional incidence constraint with certainty.
assumptions_latex: The rounded vector is integral and preserves total one.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal-and-Cardinality Insufficiency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative Cylinder Dependence of Cardinality Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset-event bounds for the stated randomized pairwise dependent-rounding process.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the output \(X\) of the stated pairwise dependent-rounding process with initial vector \(x\), every \(T\subseteq[m]\) satisfies
\[\Pr[X_i=1\ \forall i\in T]\le\prod_{i\in T}x_i,\qquad \Pr[X_i=0\ \forall i\in T]\le\prod_{i\in T}(1-x_i).\]
These cylinder inequalities support the usual Chernoff-type concentration analysis for sums of selected coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard cardinality-preserving pairwise rounding process has negative all-one and all-zero cylinder dependence.
assumptions_latex: The accepted randomized pairwise boundary-update rule is used.
The initial vector lies in \([0,1]^m\) and has integral total.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr[X_i=1\ \forall i\in T]\le\prod_{i\in T}x_i,\quad \Pr[X_i=0\ \forall i\in T]\le\prod_{i\in T}(1-x_i).
knowledge_statements.title: Negative Cylinder Dependence of Cardinality Rounding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical incidence-rounding guarantee when each ground element occurs in few selected-set columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal S\) be a finite family of subsets of a finite ground set, and suppose every ground element belongs to at most \(t\) members of \(\mathcal S\). There exists a signing \(\chi:\mathcal S\to\{-1,1\}\) such that for every ground element \(e\),
\[\left|\sum_{S\in\mathcal S:e\in S}\chi(S)\right|\le2t-1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every element occurs in at most t sets, the set-incidence columns can be signed with row discrepancy at most 2t−1.
assumptions_latex: The ground set and set family are finite.
Every element occurs in at most \(t\) sets.

notation.meaning: Maximum number of sets containing one ground element.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic scale-sample-alter template; concrete guarantees depend on the covering or packing system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\), set \(q_S=\min\{1,\alpha x_S\}\) and sample indicators \(Y_S\in\{0,1\}\) with \(\Pr(Y_S=1)=q_S\), using either independent or prescribed dependent rounding. Inspect every violated covering or packing constraint and apply a deterministic or randomized alteration that adds or deletes sets according to the problem-specific repair rule. Denote the repaired indicators by \(X_S\). Stop when all required constraints, or their declared approximation relaxations, hold, and output \(\{S\in\mathcal S:X_S=1\}\). The scaling and alteration must be analyzed jointly to bound objective loss and repair probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale fractional set choices, round them to an initial subfamily, then repair violated covering or packing constraints while controlling objective loss.

children.title: Mixed Covering–Packing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem families combining lower-bound coverage requirements with upper-bound resource restrictions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of covering-deficit and packing-overload guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X\in\{0,1\}^n be randomized, define F_i^c=\{(AX)_i<b_i\} and F_k^p=\{(CX)_k>d_k\}, and suppose \Pr[F_i^c]\le p_i and \Pr[F_k^p]\le q_k. Then \Pr[AX\ge b\text{ and }CX\le d]\ge1-\sum_i p_i-\sum_k q_k. Thus a total strictly below one certifies an integral outcome satisfying both systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Covering deficits and packing overloads must be accounted for together; a total failure bound below one certifies simultaneous feasibility.
assumptions_latex: All displayed event-probability bounds are valid; independence between constraint events is unnecessary.

notation.meaning: Failure event for covering row i.
Failure event for packing row k.

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Mixed-System Failure Accounting

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible integral solution belongs to \(\{xiction\{0,1\}^n:Ax\ge b,\ Cx\le d\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous nonnegative covering and packing constraints on one binary decision vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed covering–packing system consists of a common decision vector \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), lower-bound constraints \(Ax\ge b\), and upper-bound constraints \(Cx\le d\), where all coefficients and right-hand sides are nonnegative. Its fractional relaxation replaces integrality by \(x\in[0,1]^n\). A rounding guarantee must state both permitted deficits \(Ax\ge b-\varepsilon\) or multiplicative coverage factors and permitted overloads \(Cx\le d+\Delta\) or congestion factors; satisfying only one constraint family does not constitute mixed feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed regime imposes covering lower bounds and packing upper bounds on the same binary choices; any approximation must state violations for both families.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Covering–Packing Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible splittable multicommodity routing assigns \(f_{i,e}\ge0\) to each commodity \(i\) and edge \(e\). Define \(b_i(s_i)=d_i\), \(b_i(t_i)=-d_i\), and \(b_i(v)=0\) otherwise. For every commodity and vertex, conservation requires \(\sum_{e\in\delta^+(v)}f_{i,e}-\sum_{e\in\delta^-(v)}f_{i,e}=b_i(v)\). Shared capacities require \(\sum_i f_{i,e}\le u_e\) for every \(e\in E\). An unsplittable variant additionally requires each commodity's entire demand to use one admissible source–sink path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multicommodity routing sends each demand from its source to its sink under flow conservation, while all commodities jointly share edge capacities.

children.title: Congestion Control
children.top_down_role: Rounding guarantees focused on edge, vertex, or resource congestion.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Load Does Not Bound Realized Congestion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between expectation preservation and realized congestion control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a unit-capacity edge, let \(L=B\) with probability \(1/B\) and \(L=0\) otherwise, where \(B>1\). Then \(\mathbb E[L]=1\), but realized congestion equals \(B\) with positive probability. Expected edge-load control alone therefore gives no universal per-outcome congestion bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected load can equal capacity while rare outcomes have arbitrarily large congestion.
assumptions_latex: Only expected edge load is controlled.
No bounded-contribution or concentration hypothesis is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[L]\le c\) does not imply a universal bound on \(L/c\) in every outcome.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected Load Does Not Bound Realized Congestion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent uniform-capacity-multiplier representation of normalized congestion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite edge set \(E\), loads \(L_e\ge0\), and capacities \(c_e>0\), \(\min\{\rho:L_e\le\rho c_e\ \forall e\}=\max_{e\in E}L_e/c_e\). Thus congestion minimization is an epigraph problem with one scaled-capacity inequality per edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum normalized load is the smallest uniform capacity multiplier that makes every routed load feasible.
assumptions_latex: The edge set is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Congestion Epigraph Formulation

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite directed graph with capacities \(c_e>0\).
\(P_i\) is the selected path for commodity \(i\), whose demand is \(d_i\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity-normalized congestion for unsplittable routing obtained after path rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a selected path family \((P_i)_{i=1}^k\), define the load on edge \(e\) by \(L_e=\sum_{i=1}^k d_i\mathbf 1\{e\in P_i\}\). The congestion of the routing is \[\operatorname{cong}(P)=\max_{e\in E}\frac{L_e}{c_e}.\] Thus a routing has congestion at most \(\rho\) exactly when \(L_e\le \rho c_e\) for every \(e\in E\). If capacities and demands are integral, the definition is unchanged; integrality affects only the feasible path family, not the congestion measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Congestion is the largest ratio of routed demand to capacity over all edges; bounding congestion is equivalent to satisfying every capacity after uniform scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Congestion Control

children.title: Routing-to-Congestion Guarantees
children.top_down_role: How fractional route selection translates into integral congestion bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical conversion from a finite fractional path decomposition to one path per commodity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose commodity \(i\) has finite path weights \(\lambda_{iP}\ge0\) summing to \(d_i>0\). Independently choose one path \(P_i\) with probability \(\lambda_{iP}/d_i\) and route all demand \(d_i\) on it. The result is unsplittable, and \(\mathbb E[L_e]=\sum_i\sum_{P\ni e}\lambda_{iP}\) for every edge \(e\). The conversion uses one random path draw per positive-demand commodity, plus time to represent the chosen paths and accumulate their loads.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling one path per commodity produces an unsplittable routing and preserves every fractional edge load in expectation.
assumptions_latex: Each positive-demand commodity has a finite path decomposition of total weight \(d_i\).
Path choices are independent across commodities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[L_e]=\sum_i\sum_{P\ni e}\lambda_{iP}\) for every edge, after one draw per positive-demand commodity.

notation.meaning: fractional amount of commodity i on path P

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Path Rounding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of controlling the largest single-commodity edge contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let one commodity contribute \(b_e>0\) to edge \(e\) when its sampled path uses that edge, and suppose this occurs with probability \(1/2\). Then \(L_e\in\{0,b_e\}\), \(\mu_e=b_e/2\), and \(|L_e-\mu_e|=b_e/2\) in every outcome. Thus no uniform concentration guarantee at additive scale \(o(b_e)\) follows without further structure; useful relative bounds require the atomic contribution to be small compared with the relevant capacity or mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single large commodity creates load fluctuations on its own demand scale, limiting relative congestion concentration.
assumptions_latex: Its sampled path uses edge \(e\) with probability \(1/2\) and contributes \(b_e\) when selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rounded load can deviate from its mean by \(b_e/2\), so bounds at scale \(o(b_e)\) are impossible in general.

notation.meaning: expected rounded load on edge e

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-cost interface accompanying path rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If choosing path \(P\) for commodity \(i\) incurs cost \(d_i\sum_{e\in P}a_{i,e}\), and the path marginal is \(\lambda_{iP}/d_i\), then \(\mathbb E[\sum_i d_i\sum_{e\in P_i}a_{i,e}]=\sum_i\sum_P\lambda_{iP}\sum_{e\in P}a_{i,e}\). Independence across commodities is unnecessary for this equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correct per-commodity path marginals preserve every additive routing cost in expectation.
assumptions_latex: Routing cost is additive over commodity-edge incidences.
Commodity \(i\) chooses path \(P\) with marginal probability \(\lambda_{iP}/d_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The expected integral routing cost equals the fractional path-flow cost.

notation.meaning: per-unit cost of commodity i on edge e

assumptions_latex: Each commodity independently selects one path from a fractional path decomposition.
For every edge \(e\), the random contribution of one commodity lies in \([0,b_e]\).
The fractional expected edge load satisfies \(\mu_e\le \rho c_e\).

notation.meaning: random rounded load on edge e
largest single-commodity contribution to edge e

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent path rounding with a Bernstein tail and simultaneous edge guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_e\) be the load produced by independently choosing one path for each commodity from its fractional decomposition, and let \(\mu_e=\mathbb E[L_e]\le \rho c_e\). If every commodity contributes at most \(b_e\) to edge \(e\), then for every \(t_e\ge 0\), \[\Pr[L_e\ge \mu_e+t_e]\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{t_e^2}{2(b_e\mu_e+b_et_e/3)}\right).\] Consequently, a union bound gives the simultaneous guarantee \[\Pr[\forall e\in E:L_e<\mu_e+t_e]\ge 1-\sum_{e\in E}\exp\!\left(-\frac{t_e^2}{2(b_e\mu_e+b_et_e/3)}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent path rounding preserves fractional edge loads in expectation and converts per-edge Bernstein tails into a simultaneous congestion guarantee by a union bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Routing-to-Congestion Guarantees

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-moment invariant for rounding a fractional job assignment; independence is unnecessary for this identity, and no tail guarantee is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A(j) be an integral machine assignment satisfying \(\Pr[A(j)=i]=x_{ij}\), where \(x_{ij}\ge0\) and \(\sum_i x_{ij}=1\). For \(L_i=\sum_jp_{ij}\mathbf 1\{A(j)=i\}\), \[\mathbb E[L_i]=\sum_jp_{ij}x_{ij}.\] Hence \(\sum_jp_{ij}x_{ij}\le T\) implies \(\mathbb E[L_i]\le T\). This expectation identity alone supplies neither a deterministic nor a high-probability makespan bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite machine set \(M\), a finite job set \(J\), processing times \((p_{ij})\), and a fractional assignment \((x_{ij})\) satisfying \(x_{ij}\ge 0\) and \(\sum_{i\in M}x_{ij}=1\) for each \(j\in J\). Independently for every job \(j\), draw one machine \(A(j)\) with \(\Pr[A(j)=i]=x_{ij}\). Output the integral assignment \(A:J\to M\) and machine loads \(L_i=\sum_{j:A(j)=i}p_{ij}\). A stopping rule is unnecessary because exactly one draw is performed per job.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign each job independently to one machine according to its fractional assignment probabilities, then report the resulting integral assignment and machine loads.
