knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With the convention that a literal is true exactly when \(s_\ell=1\), the satisfaction indicator of \(C=(\ell\lor m)\) is \[q_{\ell m}=1-\frac{(1-s_\ell)(1-s_m)}4=\frac{3+s_\ell+s_m-s_\ell s_m}{4}.\] Introduce unit vectors \(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_n\), replace \(x_i\) by \(\langle v_0,v_i\rangle\), and replace \(x_ix_j\) by \(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\). Every Boolean assignment embeds through \(v_i=x_iv_0\); consequently, maximizing the weighted sum of the lifted clause expressions over the Gram constraints is an SDP relaxation and upper-bounds weighted MAX-2SAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-literal clause has an exact quadratic satisfaction formula. Lifting variables and products to Gram inner products produces an SDP upper relaxation for weighted MAX-2SAT.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Satisfiability Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clause identity and Gram lifting are correct for weighted MAX-2SAT, and the representation kind is appropriate. No source supports the formulation.

children.title: Tight Hyperplane-Rounding Instances
children.top_down_role: Instance families exhibiting extremal hyperplane-rounding performance.

assumptions_latex: A feasible unit-vector configuration is fixed.
Supported edges have nonnegative weights concentrated at, or asymptotically near, a minimizing angle \(\theta_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ratio of expected rounded weight to the corresponding SDP contribution equals, or converges to, \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp configurations for the local hyperplane inequality, without asserting SDP optimality for a graph family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider any sequence of feasible vector configurations and nonnegative weights for which \(\theta_e\to\theta_*\) uniformly over edges carrying nonzero weight. The ratio between expected hyperplane-cut weight and the same vectors' SDP objective is \[\frac{\sum_e w_e\theta_e/\pi}{\sum_e w_e(1-\cos\theta_e)/2}.\] If every supported edge has angle \(\theta_*\), this ratio is exactly \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\); under uniform convergence to \(\theta_*\), it converges to \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\). Thus such configurations are tight for the local rounding analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vector configurations whose weighted edges have the worst-case angle attain, or approach, the 0.87856 ratio between expected rounded value and SDP contribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Tight Hyperplane-Rounding Instances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf requests tight instances, but the record gives only a conditional statement about vector configurations and explicitly avoids establishing a graph family, SDP optimality, or global instance realizability. It therefore does not furnish the counterexample/instance claimed by the container.

children.title: SDP Integrality-Gap Instances
children.top_down_role: Constructions separating semidefinite values from integral cut values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit integrality-gap instances for the standard unweighted Maximum-Cut SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_n\) be the unweighted cycle of odd length \(n=2k+1\ge3\). Its maximum cut has value \(n-1\). Assign consecutive vertices unit vectors whose consecutive angular difference is \(\pi-\pi/n\). The standard Maximum-Cut SDP then has optimum \[\operatorname{SDP}(C_n)=\frac n2\left(1+\cos\frac\pi n\right).\] Hence \[\frac{\operatorname{OPT}(C_n)}{\operatorname{SDP}(C_n)}=\frac{2(n-1)}{n(1+\cos(\pi/n))}<1.\] Thus every odd cycle is a strict SDP integrality-gap instance, although the ratio tends to one as \(n\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every odd cycle has a strictly larger standard Maximum-Cut SDP value than maximum-cut value, with an explicit ratio approaching one for long cycles.
assumptions_latex: All cycle edges have unit weight.
The relaxation is the standard unit-vector Maximum-Cut SDP.
knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Cycle SDP Gap Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matching upper-bound certificate for the standard Max-Cut SDP value on an odd cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge3\) be odd and let \(X\succeq0\) satisfy \(X_{ii}=1\). For indices modulo \(n\), \[\sum_{i=1}^n X_{i,i+1}\ge -n\cos(\pi/n),\] and hence \[\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n(1-X_{i,i+1})\le\frac n2\bigl(1+\cos(\pi/n)\bigr).\] Together with the equally spaced planar-vector solution, this certifies the exact standard Max-Cut SDP value of \(C_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral cycle-correlation inequality supplies the upper bound matching the planar odd-cycle SDP solution.

notation.meaning: Feasible correlation matrix of the Max-Cut SDP.

knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Cycle Spectral SDP Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical asymptotic integrality-gap construction for the standard Maximum-Cut SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta_*\in(0,\pi)\) minimize \(2\theta/[\pi(1-\cos\theta)]\). High-dimensional spherical distance graphs whose edge weight is concentrated on pairs of unit vectors with inner product approaching \(\cos\theta_*\), followed by sufficiently fine finite weighted discretization, form graphs \(G_m\) satisfying \[\limsup_{m\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G_m)}{\operatorname{SDP}(G_m)}\le \frac{2\theta_*}{\pi(1-\cos\theta_*)}=\alpha_{GW}.\] Together with Goemans–Williamson rounding, the worst-case integral-to-SDP ratio equals \(\alpha_{GW}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite discretizations of high-dimensional spherical distance graphs have Max-Cut-to-SDP ratios approaching the Goemans–Williamson constant.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation is the standard unit-diagonal Maximum-Cut SDP.
The spherical graphs are discretized finely enough that cut and SDP values converge to their continuous counterparts.
review_flags: An authoritative locator should be added for the spherical construction and its finite-discretization theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Spherical-Graph Goemans–Williamson Gap Family

assumptions_latex: Each instance is a nonnegative weighted graph.
The relaxation is the standard unit-diagonal Maximum-Cut SDP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A family has asymptotic approximation-factor gap \(\rho\) when \(\liminf_t\operatorname{OPT}(G_t)/\operatorname{SDP}(G_t)=\rho\).

notation.meaning: Optimal integral cut value of instance \(G_t\).
Optimal value of the standard Maximum-Cut SDP.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization of integrality gaps for a maximization SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sequence \((G_t)_{t\ge1}\) with \(0<\operatorname{OPT}(G_t)\le\operatorname{SDP}(G_t)\), define \(\rho_t=\operatorname{OPT}(G_t)/\operatorname{SDP}(G_t)\in(0,1]\). It is an SDP integrality-gap family with approximation-factor gap at most \(\rho\) if \[\liminf_{t\to\infty}\rho_t\le\rho.\] Equivalently, under the reciprocal convention, its relaxation gap is at least \(1/\rho\) when \(\limsup_t\operatorname{SDP}(G_t)/\operatorname{OPT}(G_t)\ge1/\rho\). The convention must be stated because both ratios occur in the literature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDP integrality-gap family is measured by the limiting ratio of the best cut to the larger SDP optimum, or equivalently by its reciprocal.
knowledge_statements.title: SDP Integrality-Gap Instances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is only a convention for measuring an integrality gap. The terminal container calls for SDP integrality-gap instances, so a definition that asserts no actual or asymptotic instance family does not fill the leaf.

children.title: Geometry–Gap Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between vector configurations and observed relaxation gaps.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality and stability consequences of the weighted-average geometry–gap representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(\theta)=2\theta/[\pi(1-\cos\theta)]\), \(M=\operatorname*{argmin}_{0<\theta\le\pi}r(\theta)\), and let \(\lambda_e\) be the normalized positive SDP contributions. Then \(\sum_e\lambda_e r(\theta_e)\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\), with equality exactly when every edge with \(\lambda_e>0\) has \(\theta_e\in M\). For any proper open neighborhood \(U\supseteq M\), define \(\Delta_U=\inf_{\theta\notin U}r(\theta)-\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}>0\). Then \[\sum_{e:\theta_e\notin U}\lambda_e\le\frac{\sum_e\lambda_e r(\theta_e)-\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}}{\Delta_U}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality requires all positive SDP contribution to occur at minimizing angles, and near equality forces that contribution to concentrate near those angles.
assumptions_latex: The normalized weights \(\lambda_e\) arise from positive SDP edge contributions.
U is a proper open neighborhood of the minimizing-angle set M.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_e\lambda_e r(\theta_e)=\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\iff \lambda_e>0\Rightarrow\theta_e\in M,\text{ with the displayed concentration bound.}

notation.meaning: Set of angles minimizing the local Goemans–Williamson ratio.
Positive ratio gap outside the neighborhood U.

knowledge_statements.title: Extremal-Angle Equality and Concentration Criterion
Geometry–Gap Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition connecting edge-angle geometry with the rounding gap of a fixed SDP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_e=w_e(1-\cos\theta_e)/2\), let \(E_+=\{e:d_e>0\}\), and suppose \(D=\sum_{e\in E_+}d_e>0\). Setting \(\lambda_e=d_e/D\) for \(e\in E_+\) gives \(\lambda_e>0\) and \(\sum_{e\in E_+}\lambda_e=1\). Since edges outside \(E_+\) contribute zero to both the SDP objective and expected rounded weight, \[\frac{\sum_e w_e\theta_e/\pi}{\sum_e w_e(1-\cos\theta_e)/2}=\sum_{e\in E_+}\lambda_e r(\theta_e),\qquad r(\theta)=\frac{2\theta}{\pi(1-\cos\theta)}.\] Thus the rounding ratio is the SDP-contribution-weighted average of the local ratios on positive-contribution edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed feasible solution, the hyperplane-rounding ratio is the SDP-contribution-weighted average of the local angle ratios over edges having positive SDP contribution.
assumptions_latex: A feasible unit-vector solution and nonnegative edge weights are fixed.
At least one edge has positive SDP contribution.

notation.meaning: Normalized SDP-contribution weight of an edge in \(E_+\).

children.title: Hyperplane-Rounding Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes where standard hyperplane rounding loses effectiveness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of raw hyperplane rounding to preserve a standard vector balance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider four unit vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_4\in\mathbb R^3\) forming a regular tetrahedron, so \(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=-1/3\) for \(i\ne j\) and \(\sum_i v_i=0\). They are feasible for the standard vector balance constraint used in an exact-bisection SDP. For a positive-measure set of hyperplane normals near any \(v_i\), exactly one vector has positive inner product and the other three have negative inner product. Raw hyperplane rounding therefore produces a \(1\)-versus-\(3\) split with positive probability and is not feasibility preserving for a required \(2\)-versus-\(2\) bisection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A balanced tetrahedral SDP configuration can round to a one-versus-three split, so an unconditioned hyperplane does not preserve exact bisection.
assumptions_latex: The constrained SDP requires unit vectors satisfying \(\sum_i v_i=0\).
The integral output must contain exactly two vertices on each side.
Rounding uses one unconditioned random hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Bisection Feasibility Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic output limitation for multiway partition requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A single hyperplane through the origin assigns every input vector according to one of two signs and therefore produces at most two nonempty labels. Consequently, it cannot directly return a feasible partition required to have \(k>2\) nonempty labeled parts; additional hyperplanes, a different partition rule, or a repair procedure are necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One hyperplane creates at most two nonempty parts and therefore cannot directly satisfy a genuinely multiway nonempty-part requirement.
assumptions_latex: The output labels are determined solely by the two hyperplane signs.
The target requires k>2 nonempty parts.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Hyperplane Label-Count Boundary

assumptions_latex: The target problem requires every output part to satisfy a prescribed nonempty cardinality.
Rounding uses one unconditioned random hyperplane and assigns vertices only by its two signs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Raw hyperplane rounding is not a feasibility-preserving conversion for exact-balance or general multiway partition constraints.

notation.meaning: Vertices assigned to the two hyperplane sides.
Required size of the positive side.
Common vector assigned to every vertex in the counterexample.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility failure under side constraints, rather than failure of unconstrained Maximum-Cut approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a feasible output must satisfy \(|S_+|=b\) with \(0<b<|V|\). Assign the same unit vector \(u\) to every vertex. For every random hyperplane whose normal is not orthogonal to \(u\), all vertices receive the same sign, so \[(|S_+|,|S_-|)\in\{(|V|,0),(0,|V|)\}.\] Thus the balance constraint fails with probability one. Moreover, a single hyperplane produces only two labels and therefore cannot directly realize a required partition into \(k>2\) nonempty parts. Additional rounding and repair mechanisms are necessary in these regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A raw random hyperplane can violate exact balance with probability one and creates only two labels, so it does not directly handle constrained multiway partitions.
knowledge_statements.title: Hyperplane-Rounding Failure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-label obstruction is correct, but the exact-balance example is not shown to arise from a feasible solution of any specified constrained SDP. A source and a precise relaxation domain are needed before treating it as a conversion failure.

children.title: Maximum k-Cut SDP Rounding
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite rounding families for maximum k-cut objectives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local test deriving an approximation ratio from a specified rounding rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_k(\rho)=\Pr[\ell(i)\ne\ell(j)\mid\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=\rho]\). If \[p_k(\rho)\ge \alpha\frac{k-1}{k}(1-\rho)\] for every \(\rho\in[-1/(k-1),1]\), then every feasible SDP solution satisfies \[\mathbb E[W_{\mathrm{cut}}]\ge\alpha\operatorname{SDP}(v)\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}_{k\text{-cut}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform pairwise separation inequality certifies a Maximum k-Cut approximation factor.
assumptions_latex: Pair separation probability depends only on the corresponding SDP inner product.
The inequality holds throughout the feasible correlation interval.

notation.meaning: Probability that a pair of correlation rho receives different labels.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Value Certification by Edge Separation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Threshold Repetition from a Bounded Rounded Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum k-Cut repetition bound obtained from expected value and a deterministic objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose one rounding trial produces \(0\le W\le U\), \(\operatorname{OPT}>0\), and \(\mathbb E[W]\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\). For \(0\le\beta<\alpha\), let \[q=\frac{(\alpha-\beta)\operatorname{OPT}}{U-\beta\operatorname{OPT}}.\] Then \(U>\beta\operatorname{OPT}\) and \[\Pr(W\ge\beta\operatorname{OPT})\ge q.\] Consequently, the best of \(t\) independent trials misses this threshold with probability at most \((1-q)^t\le e^{-qt}\), and rejection sampling needs at most \(1/q\) trials in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic upper bound converts an expected cut guarantee into a threshold-success probability and repetition bound.

notation.meaning: Rounded cut weight in one trial.
Deterministic upper bound, such as total edge weight.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Repetition from a Bounded Rounded Value

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perfect Gaussian-Rounding Factor Fails for k=2
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit feasible correlation at which Gaussian rounding does not attain the SDP edge value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k=2\) and \(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=-1/2\), Gaussian-argmax rounding is random-hyperplane rounding, so \[p_2(-1/2)=\frac{\arccos(-1/2)}{\pi}=\frac23.\] The unit-weight SDP edge contribution is \(\frac12(1+1/2)=3/4\). Hence its separation-to-SDP ratio is \(8/9<1\), so this rounding rule has no uniform factor-one guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At correlation minus one half, the separation probability is two thirds while the SDP edge contribution is three quarters.
assumptions_latex: The edge has unit weight and endpoint correlation \(-1/2\).

notation.meaning: Pair-separation probability for two-label Gaussian rounding.

knowledge_statements.title: Perfect Gaussian-Rounding Factor Fails for k=2

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual of the Maximum k-Cut SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual upper-bound certificate including every pairwise lower-correlation constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c=(k-1)/k\), \(b=1/(k-1)\), \(A^{ij}=(e_ie_j^{\mathsf T}+e_je_i^{\mathsf T})/2\), and \(C=c\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}\). For the primal \[\max_{X\succeq0}\ C-c\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}\langle A^{ij},X\rangle\quad\text{s.t. }X_{ii}=1,\ \langle A^{ij},X\rangle\ge-b\ (i<j),\] the dual is \[\min_{y,\,z\ge0}\ C+\sum_i y_i+b\sum_{i<j}z_{ij}\] subject to \[\operatorname{Diag}(y)-\sum_{i<j}z_{ij}A^{ij}+c\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}A^{ij}\succeq0.\] Every dual-feasible \((y,z)\) certifies its objective as an upper bound on both the SDP optimum and the maximum k-cut optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal and nonnegative pair variables, together with a positive-semidefinite slack matrix, give an SDP upper-bound certificate.
assumptions_latex: The matrix inner product is the trace inner product.

notation.meaning: Dual variable for the unit-diagonal equality.
Nonnegative dual variable for a lower-correlation constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual of the Maximum k-Cut SDP

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected approximation factor of Gaussian-argmax rounding for the standard Maximum k-Cut SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\ge2\), let \(p_k(\rho)\) be the probability that two unit vectors of inner product \(\rho\) receive different labels under Gaussian-argmax rounding, and define \[\alpha_k=\inf_{-1/(k-1)\le\rho<1}\frac{p_k(\rho)}{\frac{k-1}{k}(1-\rho)}.\] Then \[\mathbb E[W_{\mathrm{cut}}]\ge\alpha_k\operatorname{SDP}(v)\ge\alpha_k\operatorname{OPT}_{k\text{-cut}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Frieze–Jerrum factor is the worst feasible-correlation ratio of Gaussian separation probability to SDP edge contribution.
assumptions_latex: The graph is undirected with nonnegative edge weights.
The SDP vectors are unit vectors with inner products at least \(-1/(k-1)\).
Labels are assigned by Gaussian-argmax rounding.
knowledge_statements.title: Frieze–Jerrum Gaussian-Rounding Factor

assumptions_latex: The graph is undirected with nonnegative weights and \(k\ge2\).
An optimal feasible Gram matrix for the displayed SDP is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a random partition into at most \(k\) classes whose expected value is determined by pairwise Gaussian comparison probabilities.

notation.meaning: Independent standard Gaussian direction for label \(a\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian argmax rounding for the standard Maximum k-Cut SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve \[\max\frac{k-1}{k}\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)\] subject to \(\|v_i\|=1\) and \(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\ge-1/(k-1)\) for all \(i,j\). Independently sample \(g_1,\ldots,g_k\) from the standard Gaussian distribution in the vector span and assign \[\ell(i)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{1\le a\le k}\langle g_a,v_i\rangle,\] resolving zero-probability ties by the smallest label. Output the classes \(S_a=\{i:\ell(i)=a\}\); stop after this single rounding step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the standard Maximum k-Cut SDP, sample one Gaussian direction per label, and assign each vertex to the direction having the largest projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum k-Cut SDP Rounding

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf and the SDP plus Gaussian-argmax rule is stated precisely, but no citation supports this particular relaxation-rounding pairing or its performance interpretation.

children.title: Multiway Graph Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Rounding structures for partitions with multiple vertex classes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating principal multiway partition variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A common labeling \(\ell:V\to[k]\) does not make Maximum \(k\)-Cut, terminal Multiway Cut, and balanced partitioning interchangeable: the first maximizes crossing weight, the second minimizes it subject to \(\ell(t_a)=a\), and the third adds cardinality or volume constraints. A guarantee transfers only when the target feasibility constraints and objective direction are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared labeling representation does not transfer approximation guarantees among maximum-cut, terminal, and balanced variants.
assumptions_latex: The variants use the same weighted graph and label set.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-and-Constraint Noninterchangeability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical vector representation of a k-way labeling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_1,\ldots,u_k\) be centered regular-simplex vertices with \(\|u_a\|=1\) and \(\langle u_a,u_b\rangle=-1/(k-1)\) for \(a\ne b\). For \(v_i=u_{\ell(i)}\), \[\mathbf1[\ell(i)\ne\ell(j)]=\frac{k-1}{k}(1-\langle v_i,v_j\rangle).\] Thus crossing-weight objectives have an exact integral Gram representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regular-simplex label vectors represent pair separation by an affine function of their inner product.
assumptions_latex: Every vertex receives exactly one label.

notation.meaning: Vector representing the label of vertex i.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Pair-Separation Identity

assumptions_latex: The graph is undirected with nonnegative edge weights.
Each vertex must receive one of \(k\) labels.
Any terminal or balance requirements are stated as explicit feasibility constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible labeling induces the partition \((S_1,\ldots,S_k)\) and crossing weight \(\sum_{\{i,j\}}w_{ij}\mathbf1[\ell(i)\ne\ell(j)]\).

notation.meaning: Total weight crossing between distinct parts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common labeling model covering maximum k-cut and constrained multiway partition variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A \(k\)-way graph partition is a labeling \(\ell:V\to[k]\) with parts \(S_a=\{i\in V:\ell(i)=a\}\). Its crossing weight is \[W_{\mathrm{cross}}(\ell)=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}\mathbf1[\ell(i)\ne\ell(j)].\] Maximum \(k\)-Cut maximizes this quantity without requiring every \(S_a\) to be nonempty. Terminal multiway cut instead prescribes distinct terminals \(t_a\) with \(\ell(t_a)=a\) and minimizes the same quantity. Balanced variants additionally impose lower or upper bounds on \(|S_a|\) or weighted part volumes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiway partition is a vertex labeling. Different problem variants maximize or minimize crossing weight and may impose terminal, nonemptiness, or balance constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiway Graph Partitioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The labeling definition correctly distinguishes maximum k-cut, terminal multiway cut, and balanced variants. It lacks an inspectable source locator.

children.title: Label-Based Partition Rounding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility supplied by any total label assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every total map \(\ell:V\to[k]\), the sets \(S_a=\ell^{-1}(a)\) are pairwise disjoint and satisfy \(\bigcup_{a=1}^kS_a=V\). They form exactly \(k\) nonempty classes if and only if \(\ell\) is surjective.

assumptions_latex: Every vertex receives exactly one label in \([k]\).

Label-Based Partition Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic Gaussian label rounding; terminal and balance constraints may require conditioning or repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input feasible label vectors \(v_{i,a}\) for \(i\in V\) and \(a\in[k]\). Independently sample standard Gaussian vectors \(g_1,\ldots,g_k\) in their common span. Compute \(s_{i,a}=\langle g_a,v_{i,a}\rangle\) and set \[\ell(i)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{a\in[k]}s_{i,a},\] breaking ties by the smallest label. Output \(S_a=\{i:\ell(i)=a\}\). The generic rule assigns exactly one label to every vertex; prescribed terminals, nonempty classes, or balance bounds require a variant-specific conditioning or repair step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian label rounding scores every vertex-label vector and assigns each vertex its highest-scoring label; side constraints require a compatible repair or conditioning step.
assumptions_latex: For every vertex \(i\) and label \(a\), a vector \(v_{i,a}\) is supplied by an SDP relaxation.
The Gaussian score rule is compatible with the relaxation's required feasibility constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell(i)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{a\in[k]}\langle g_a,v_{i,a}\rangle\) assigns one label to every vertex.

Independent standard Gaussian vector associated with label \(a\).

children.title: Unbalanced Partition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Partitioning variants without prescribed balance constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbalanced Partition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the small-part-mass formulation for weighted multiway partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) have vertex weights \(w_v\ge 0\), total weight \(W=\sum_{v\in V}w_v>0\), and let \((P_1,\ldots,P_k)\) partition \(V\). For \(0<\varepsilon<1/k\), the partition is in the \(\varepsilon\)-unbalanced regime when
\[\min_{1\le i\le k} w(P_i)\le \varepsilon W,\qquad w(P_i)=\sum_{v\in P_i}w_v.\]
A rounding guarantee specialized to this regime may depend explicitly on \(\varepsilon\), since a multiplicative bound on the smallest part does not provide a uniform lower bound on every part mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted multiway partition is epsilon-unbalanced when at least one part contains at most an epsilon fraction of the total vertex weight.

notation.meaning: Total vertex weight of a subset S.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted small-part definition is mathematically coherent and fits the regime container, but no inspectable source supports this particular meaning of “unbalanced” or the accompanying rounding-guarantee claim.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of the positive-semidefinite multiplicative comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The arcsine identity remains exact for symmetric indefinite objectives, but the \(2/\pi\) comparison can fail. Already for \(n=1\) and \(Q=[-1]\), the unique feasible correlation matrix is \(X=[1]\) and every rounded sign has objective \(-1\), whereas \((2/\pi)\langle Q,X\rangle=-2/\pi\); hence \(-1\ge-2/\pi\) is false. Multiplicative approximation is also unsuitable when the chosen normalization permits a nonpositive optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-variable negative quadratic form shows that the arcsine identity does not yield the 2/pi inequality without positive semidefiniteness.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric but not assumed positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\not\succeq0\not\Rightarrow\mathbb E[\widehat x^{\mathsf T}Q\widehat x]\ge(2/\pi)\langle Q,X\rangle.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual upper-bound certificate for homogeneous binary quadratic maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dual of \[\max\{\langle Q,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1\}\] is \[\min\left\{\sum_i y_i:\operatorname{Diag}(y)-Q\succeq0\right\}.\] Every dual-feasible \(y\) upper-bounds every binary quadratic solution; equality of feasible primal and dual objectives certifies SDP optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagonal matrix dominating Q in semidefinite order certifies an upper bound on every binary quadratic solution.

notation.meaning: Dual vector for the unit-diagonal constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nesterov-type guarantee for positive-semidefinite binary quadratic maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succeq0\), let \(X\) optimize \(\max\{\langle Q,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1\}\), and apply Gaussian hyperplane rounding. Then \[\mathbb E[\widehat x^{\mathsf T}Q\widehat x]\ge\frac{2}{\pi}\langle Q,X\rangle\ge\frac{2}{\pi}\max_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}x^{\mathsf T}Qx.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-semidefinite quadratic form, Gaussian hyperplane rounding is a 2/pi approximation.
assumptions_latex: The correlation SDP is solved optimally.
Rounding uses a standard Gaussian hyperplane.

Quadratic-Program Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian hyperplane rounding for a binary homogeneous quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given symmetric \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), relax \(\max\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx:x\in\{-1,1\}^n\}\) to
\[\max\{\langle Q,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1\ (i\in[n])\}.\]
Compute an optimal feasible Gram matrix \(X_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\), sample \(g\sim N(0,I)\), and output \(\widehat x_i=\operatorname{sign}\langle g,v_i\rangle\), using either sign at zero. Then
\[\mathbb E[\widehat x_i\widehat x_j]=\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin(X_{ij}),\]
so the rounded expected objective is obtained by applying this entrywise correlation conversion to \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the correlation-matrix SDP, cut its Gram vectors by a random Gaussian hyperplane, and evaluate the resulting signs through the arcsine correlation identity.
assumptions_latex: The semidefinite relaxation is solved to the desired numerical accuracy.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted complete-graph minimum-disagreement correlation clustering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On an unweighted complete signed graph, repeatedly choose a uniformly random remaining pivot \(p\), output the cluster containing \(p\) and all its remaining positive neighbors, and delete that cluster. For the resulting partition \(C\), \[\mathbb E[\operatorname{dis}(C)]\le3\operatorname{OPT}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random pivoting is a 3-approximation for unweighted complete-graph minimum-disagreement correlation clustering.
assumptions_latex: Every unordered vertex pair has sign \(+\) or \(-\).
Each pivot is uniform among the remaining vertices.
knowledge_statements.title: Random-Pivot Three-Approximation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit boundary for agreement–disagreement complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the all-positive complete graph \(K_n\), the one-cluster partition has \(\operatorname{dis}=0\). A partition separating one vertex has \(\operatorname{dis}=n-1\) but agreement ratio \((n-2)/n\) relative to the maximum agreement value \(\binom n2\). Thus agreement ratios can approach one while no finite multiplicative disagreement ratio relative to the zero optimum is obtained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an all-positive clique, a nearly optimal agreement solution can have positive disagreement although the optimum disagreement is zero.
assumptions_latex: Every pair has unit weight and positive sign.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicative-Ratio Nontransfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of objectives on a fixed complete signed instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=\sum_{\{u,v\}}w_{uv}\). For every partition \(\mathcal P\), \[\operatorname{agr}(\mathcal P)+\operatorname{dis}(\mathcal P)=W.\] Hence maximizing agreements and minimizing disagreements have the same exact optimizers, although multiplicative approximation ratios do not transfer through this additive identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agreements and disagreements sum to the total pair weight, but their multiplicative approximation ratios are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: The signed weighted instance is fixed and complete.
knowledge_statements.title: Agreement–Disagreement Complementarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral pair-separation representation of correlation clustering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Put \(x_{uv}=1\) when \(u,v\) lie in different blocks and \(x_{uv}=0\) otherwise. These variables form a symmetric \(\{0,1\}\)-semimetric, and conversely every such semimetric defines a partition by \(u\sim v\iff x_{uv}=0\). Thus minimum disagreements is \[\min\left\{\sum_{uv\in E^+}w_{uv}x_{uv}+\sum_{uv\in E^-}w_{uv}(1-x_{uv}):x\text{ is a }\{0,1\}\text{-semimetric}\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitions correspond exactly to zero-one semimetrics, making disagreement a linear pair-separation objective.
assumptions_latex: The instance is complete and has nonnegative pair weights.

notation.meaning: Indicator that u and v are separated.

knowledge_statements.title: Semimetric Disagreement Formulation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation certificate based on a validated lower bound for the semimetric relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a certified lower bound satisfying \(B\le L^*\), where \(L^*\) is the optimum of the triangle-inequality relaxation. If an integral partition \(\mathcal P\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dis}(\mathcal P)\le\rho B\), then \[\operatorname{dis}(\mathcal P)\le\rho\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{dis}}.\] A feasible dual solution of the relaxation is one standard way to certify such a value \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition costing at most rho times a certified relaxation lower bound is a rho-approximation.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound on the fractional relaxation optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Disagreement Lower-Bound Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical fractional semimetric relaxation for complete-graph minimum-disagreement correlation clustering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Relax the integral separation variables to \(0\le x_{uv}\le1\) and impose \(x_{uv}\le x_{uw}+x_{wv}\) for all distinct \(u,v,w\). Minimizing \[\sum_{uv\in E^+}w_{uv}x_{uv}+\sum_{uv\in E^-}w_{uv}(1-x_{uv})\] over these fractional semimetrics is a linear-programming relaxation of minimum disagreements. Its optimum \(L^*\) therefore satisfies \(L^*\le\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{dis}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractional pair distances satisfying triangle inequalities give the standard LP lower bound for minimum disagreements.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the triangle-inequality LP.

knowledge_statements.title: Triangle-Inequality LP Relaxation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit lower-bound dual for the shifted fractional-semimetric LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Index unordered pairs by \(e\), put \(c_e=w_e\) for positive pairs and \(c_e=-w_e\) for negative pairs, and let \(W^-=\sum_{e\in E^-}w_e\). Write the triangle inequalities as \(Ax\le0\). The primal minimizes \(W^-+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\le0\) and \(0\le x\le1\). An equivalent dual is
\[\max_{y,z\ge0}\left\{W^- -\sum_e z_e:(-A)^Ty-z\le c\right\}.\]
Every feasible \((y,z)\) therefore certifies \(W^- -\sum_ez_e\le L^*\le\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{dis}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative multipliers for triangle inequalities and distance upper bounds give a checkable lower bound on minimum disagreements.
assumptions_latex: The signed instance is complete and has nonnegative weights.
The matrix \(A\) contains the chosen inequalities \(x_{uv}-x_{uw}-x_{wv}\le0\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient matrix of the oriented triangle inequalities.
Nonnegative dual multipliers for the negated triangle inequalities.
Nonnegative dual multipliers for upper bounds on pair distances.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual of the Triangle-Inequality Relaxation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementation and repetition bounds for unweighted complete-graph Random Pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With a signed adjacency matrix, one Random-Pivot run can be implemented in \(O(n^2)\) time and \(O(n)\) auxiliary space. Since \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{dis}(C)]\le3\operatorname{OPT}\), Markov's inequality gives \(\Pr[\operatorname{dis}(C)\le6\operatorname{OPT}]\ge1/2\). Running independently \(r=\lceil\log_2(1/\delta)\rceil\) times and returning the least-disagreement partition yields a \(6\)-approximation with probability at least \(1-\delta\) in \(O(rn^2)\) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random Pivot runs in quadratic time; logarithmically many independent repetitions give a 6-approximation with high probability.
assumptions_latex: The instance is an unweighted complete signed graph represented by constant-time sign queries.
Independent runs use independent pivot choices.
knowledge_statements.title: Random-Pivot Runtime and Constant-Probability Amplification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite strengthening of the pair-separation relaxation for complete-graph minimum-disagreement correlation clustering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Introduce a symmetric matrix \(Y\in\mathbb S^{V}\) and set \(x_{uv}=1-Y_{uv}\). Minimize
\[\sum_{uv\in E^+}w_{uv}x_{uv}+\sum_{uv\in E^-}w_{uv}(1-x_{uv})\]
subject to
\[Y\succeq0,\qquad Y_{uu}=1,\qquad 0\le Y_{uv}\le1,\qquad x_{uv}\le x_{uw}+x_{wv}\quad(u,v,w\in V).\]
Every partition embeds by assigning mutually orthogonal unit vectors to distinct blocks and taking \(Y\) as their Gram matrix. Therefore the SDP optimum lower-bounds minimum disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonal block vectors give a positive-semidefinite strengthening of the fractional semimetric relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The signed instance is complete and all pair weights are nonnegative.

notation.meaning: Positive-semidefinite Gram matrix of relaxed cluster vectors.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Signed-Graph Reduction to Zero-Weight Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact objective-preserving representation of absent pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an incomplete signed graph \(H=(V,E^+\cup E^-)\) with nonnegative weights, complete the instance by assigning weight zero and an arbitrary sign to every absent pair. Every partition \(\mathcal P\) then has the same agreement and disagreement values in \(H\) and its completion. Thus incomplete correlation clustering is an exact zero-weight specialization of the weighted complete formulation, although an approximation theorem with stronger weight hypotheses does not transfer automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absent pairs are represented exactly by zero-weight pairs in a complete signed instance.
assumptions_latex: Observed positive and negative pair sets are disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dis}_H(\mathcal P)=\operatorname{dis}_{\overline H_0}(\mathcal P)\quad\text{for every partition }\mathcal P.

notation.meaning: A complete zero-weight extension of the incomplete instance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition and obstruction extraction for unweighted complete signed graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute the connected components of \(G^+=(V,E^+)\). If each component is a positive clique, return these components as a zero-disagreement partition. Otherwise choose a negative pair joined by a shortest positive path; the first two edges of a shortest subpath together with its negative chord give a triangle with exactly two positive edges. With constant-time sign queries this takes \(O(n^2)\) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive components either form a perfect clustering or expose a two-positive-one-negative triangle.
assumptions_latex: Every unordered pair has unit weight and sign \(+\) or \(-\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A zero-disagreement partition or a signed-triangle obstruction is returned in }O(n^2)\text{ time}.
knowledge_statements.title: Perfect-Clusterability Recognition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact zero-optimum characterization for unweighted complete signed instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an unweighted complete signed graph, \[\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{dis}}=0\Longleftrightarrow G^+\text{ is a disjoint union of cliques}\Longleftrightarrow\text{no triangle has exactly two positive edges}.\] When these conditions hold, the components of \(G^+\) are a zero-disagreement partition; otherwise such a triangle certifies positive optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfect clusterability is equivalent to transitivity of the positive relation.
assumptions_latex: Every unordered pair has unit weight and sign \(+\) or \(-\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{dis}}=0\Longleftrightarrow E^+\text{ is a disjoint union of cliques}.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Disagreement Clusterability Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General signed-graph minimum-disagreement regime, including incomplete instances and zero-weight complete representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a signed graph on \(n\) vertices with disjoint positive and negative edge sets and nonnegative rational weights, there is a polynomial-time rounding algorithm for the triangle-inequality semimetric relaxation that returns a partition \(\mathcal P\) satisfying \[\operatorname{dis}(\mathcal P)\le O(\log n)\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{dis}}.\] Thus the guarantee applies to incomplete signed graphs and to their objective-equivalent zero-weight completions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The semimetric LP admits a polynomial-time logarithmic approximation for general weighted, possibly incomplete, minimum-disagreement correlation clustering.
assumptions_latex: The positive and negative edge sets are disjoint.
All edge weights are nonnegative rationals.
The fractional semimetric relaxation is solved to sufficient polynomial precision.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-optimum characterization for arbitrary nonnegative pair weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Discard zero-weight pairs and let \(G_+^w\) contain the positive-sign pairs of positive weight. The instance has zero disagreement if and only if no negative-sign pair of positive weight has both endpoints in one connected component of \(G_+^w\). When this holds, the components of \(G_+^w\) form a zero-disagreement partition. Otherwise, a positive path joining the endpoints of a positive-weight negative pair witnesses impossibility of zero disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-weight must-link components may not contain a positive-weight cannot-link pair; this exactly characterizes zero weighted disagreement.
assumptions_latex: All represented pair weights are nonnegative.
Each represented pair has a positive or negative sign.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{dis}}=0\Longleftrightarrow\forall uv\in E^-\text{ with }w_{uv}>0,\ u,v\text{ lie in distinct components of }G_+^w.

notation.meaning: Graph of positive-sign pairs having positive weight.

Correlation Clustering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted disagreement minimization on a signed complete graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be finite, and assign each unordered pair \(\{u,v\}\) a nonnegative weight \(w_{uv}\) and sign \(\sigma_{uv}\in\{+,-\}\). For a partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(V\), a positive pair disagrees when its endpoints lie in distinct blocks, while a negative pair disagrees when they lie in the same block. The correlation-clustering disagreement objective is
\[\operatorname{dis}(\mathcal P)=\sum_{\sigma_{uv}=+}w_{uv}\mathbf 1[u\not\sim_{\mathcal P}v]+\sum_{\sigma_{uv}=-}w_{uv}\mathbf 1[u\sim_{\mathcal P}v].\]
Minimum-disagreement correlation clustering asks for a partition minimizing this quantity, with no prescribed number of blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correlation clustering partitions signed, weighted vertices while minimizing positive edges cut plus negative edges retained inside clusters.

notation.meaning: Vertices u and v belong to the same partition block.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical semidefinite feasibility relaxation underlying graph-coloring rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(k\ge2\), a strict vector \(k\)-coloring assigns unit vectors \(v_u\) satisfying \[\langle v_u,v_v\rangle=-\frac1{k-1}\qquad(\{u,v\}\in E).\] Replacing equality by \(\langle v_u,v_v\rangle\le-1/(k-1)\) gives the vector \(k\)-coloring relaxation. Every proper \(k\)-coloring yields a strict vector coloring by assigning regular-simplex vertices to its color classes; consequently the least feasible vector-coloring parameter is at most \(\chi(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper k-coloring embeds as regular-simplex vectors, giving a semidefinite relaxation of chromatic number.

notation.meaning: Least feasible parameter for the stated non-strict vector-coloring relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Vector-Coloring Relaxation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized SDP-based coloring of graphs promised to be k-colorable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every fixed integer \(k\ge3\), there is a randomized polynomial-time algorithm which, given an \(n\)-vertex graph known to be \(k\)-colorable, computes a proper coloring using \[O\!\left(n^{1-3/(k+1)}\sqrt{\log n}\right)\] colors with high probability. In particular, a 3-colorable graph receives \(O(n^{1/4}\sqrt{\log n})\) colors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SDP vector-coloring methods properly color a k-colorable graph with O(n^(1−3/(k+1)) sqrt(log n)) colors for fixed k.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite simple graph on \(n\) vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{With high probability, the output is proper and uses }O\!\left(n^{1-3/(k+1)}\sqrt{\log n}\right)\text{ colors}.

notation.meaning: Promised upper bound on the chromatic number.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-controlled rounding of vector colorings; it does not itself ensure a proper coloring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Draw independent \(g_1,\ldots,g_t\sim N(0,I)\) and set \(c(u)=(\operatorname{sign}\langle g_1,v_u\rangle,\ldots,\operatorname{sign}\langle g_t,v_u\rangle)\). For \(\theta_{uv}=\arccos\langle v_u,v_v\rangle\), \[\Pr[c(u)=c(v)]=\left(1-\frac{\theta_{uv}}{\pi}\right)^t,\qquad \mathbb E|F_c|=\sum_{uv\in E}\left(1-\frac{\theta_{uv}}{\pi}\right)^t.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated Gaussian hyperplanes give at most 2^t labels and an exact angular formula for expected monochromatic edges.
assumptions_latex: The vectors \(v_u\) are unit vectors in one Euclidean space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict and non-strict vector-coloring consequences for repeated-hyperplane rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every edge satisfies \(\langle v_u,v_v\rangle=-1/(k-1)\), then its collision probability is \[p_{k,t}=\left(1-\pi^{-1}\arccos\left(-\frac1{k-1}\right)\right)^t\] and \(\mathbb E|F_c|=|E|p_{k,t}\). If instead \(\langle v_u,v_v\rangle\le-1/(k-1)\), these become upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict vector constraints give exact uniform conflict probabilities; non-strict constraints give the same upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The vectors form a strict or non-strict vector \(k\)-coloring.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E|F_c|\le |E|p_{k,t},\text{ with equality in the strict case}.

notation.meaning: Per-edge collision bound after t hyperplanes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Hyperplane Rounding Can Leave Conflicts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-probability obstruction to obtaining a proper coloring directly from finitely many hyperplanes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_3\) have its strict vector \(3\)-coloring by three unit vectors with pairwise inner product \(-1/2\). Under \(t\ge1\) independent Gaussian hyperplanes, every fixed edge \(uv\) is monochromatic with probability \[\left(1-\pi^{-1}\arccos(-1/2)\right)^t=3^{-t}>0.\] Hence the rounded labeling fails to be proper with positive probability for every finite \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even the simplex vectors for a triangle leave a fixed edge monochromatic with positive probability after any finite number of hyperplanes.
assumptions_latex: The vectors form the regular-simplex strict vector \(3\)-coloring.

notation.meaning: Set of monochromatic edges after rounding.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local recursive conversion from a sibling-owned independent-set extractor to a proper coloring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\mathcal A\), on every \(m\)-vertex induced subgraph in a hereditary graph class, returns an independent set of size at least \(s(m)\) with probability at least \(p>0\), where \(s(m)\ge1\) is nondecreasing. At each residual graph, run \(\mathcal A\) independently \(R=\lceil p^{-1}\ln(n/\delta)\rceil\) times, retain a candidate only after verifying both independence and size at least \(s(m)\), assign a new color to one retained set, and delete it; declare failure if no attempt qualifies. With probability at least \(1-\delta\), the procedure does not fail and returns a proper coloring using at most \(\sum_{m=1}^n1/s(m)\) colors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly verify and remove sufficiently large independent sets; with amplified confidence this yields a proper coloring whose color count is controlled by the extractor size.
assumptions_latex: The graph class is closed under induced subgraphs.
Each candidate is checked for independence and cardinality before deletion.
Extraction attempts are independent and have success probability at least \(p>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr\!\left[\text{a proper coloring with at most }\sum_{m=1}^n s(m)^{-1}\text{ colors is returned}\right]\ge1-\delta.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Runtime Composition for Verified Recursive Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional runtime of the accepted independent-set-to-coloring conversion, without asserting a KMS implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that on an \(m\)-vertex residual graph one relaxation solve costs \(S(m)\), one extraction attempt together with independence-and-size verification costs \(E(m)\), and at most \(R\) attempts are made before deleting a nonempty verified independent set. If \(G_m\) denotes the residual graph at such a stage and \(\mathcal M\) the sequence of residual sizes, then \[T\le\sum_{m\in\mathcal M}\bigl(S(m)+R E(m)+O(m+|E(G_m)|)\bigr),\qquad |\mathcal M|\le n.\] Thus polynomial \(S,E\) and \(R=O(\log(n/\delta))\) give randomized polynomial total time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified recursive extraction is polynomial-time when every residual relaxation and extraction attempt is polynomial-time and only logarithmically many retries are used.
assumptions_latex: Every deleted set is nonempty and is verified to be independent and sufficiently large.
At most \(R\) extraction attempts occur at each residual stage.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let unit vectors \(v_u\) represent vertices of \(G=(V,E)\), and fix \(q\ge2\). Draw independent \(g_1,\ldots,g_q\sim N(0,I)\) and assign
\[c(u)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{a\in[q]}\langle g_a,v_u\rangle,\]
using a fixed rule for ties. Output the labeling \(c:V\to[q]\) together with the conflict set \(F_c=\{\{u,v\}\in E:c(u)=c(v)\}\). If \(F_c=\varnothing\), then \(c\) is a proper \(q\)-coloring; otherwise the rounding is evaluated by \(\mathbb E[w(F_c)]\) or followed by an explicitly specified conflict-repair procedure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual certificate corresponding to the trace-one primal theta normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(G=(V,E)\), let \(E^{uv}\) be the symmetric matrix with ones in positions \((u,v)\) and \((v,u)\). The primal \[\max\{\langle J,X\rangle:\operatorname{Tr}X=1,\ X_{uv}=0\ (uv\in E),\ X\succeq0\}\] has dual \[\min\left\{t:tI+\sum_{uv\in E}y_{uv}E^{uv}-J\succeq0\right\}.\] Primal strict feasibility gives strong duality, and every dual-feasible \((t,y)\) certifies \(\vartheta(G)\le t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite dual matrix gives a checkable upper certificate for the theta value.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual SDP Form of Lovász Theta

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical placement of theta between independence and complementary coloring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite simple graph \(G\), \[\alpha(G)\le\vartheta(G)\le\chi(\overline G).\] Equivalently, applying the statement to the complement gives \(\omega(G)\le\vartheta(\overline G)\le\chi(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lovász theta lies between the independence number and the chromatic number of the complement.
knowledge_statements.title: Lovász Theta Sandwich Theorem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak polynomial-time computation of the displayed theta SDP to additive accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite simple graph \(G\) and rational \(\varepsilon>0\), the trace-one theta SDP can be solved to additive objective accuracy \(\varepsilon\) in time polynomial in the graph encoding length and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\), using standard rational semidefinite-programming algorithms. Rational approximate primal and dual solutions can be returned with explicitly bounded feasibility and objective residuals. Exact algebraic computation is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lovász theta is approximable to prescribed additive accuracy in polynomial bit complexity.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite simple graph represented explicitly.
The standard weak bit-complexity model for rational semidefinite programming is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \vartheta(G)\text{ is computable to additive error }\varepsilon\text{ in time polynomial in the input length and }\log(1/\varepsilon).
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Time Approximation of Lovász Theta
Independent-Set SDP Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lovász-theta upper bound in a primal SDP normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite simple graph \(G=(V,E)\), define
\[\vartheta(G)=\max\left\{\langle J,X\rangle:\operatorname{Tr}(X)=1,\ X_{uv}=0\ \text{for }\{u,v\}\in E,\ X\succeq0\right\}.\]
Every independent set \(S\subseteq V\) gives the feasible matrix \(X=|S|^{-1}\mathbf1_S\mathbf1_S^{\mathsf T}\), whose objective value is \(|S|\). Consequently,
\[\alpha(G)\le \vartheta(G).\]
Thus this semidefinite program supplies a polynomial-time computable upper bound on the maximum independent-set cardinality, up to the numerical accuracy used to solve the SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lovász theta SDP upper-bounds the independence number because every independent set induces a feasible rank-one matrix of equal value.

notation.meaning: Lovász theta value in the displayed normalization.

children.title: Coloring–Stable-Set Relations
children.top_down_role: Structural connections between coloring certificates and stable-set bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fractional coloring as a stable-set cover and its finite LP dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the stable-set family \(\mathcal S\) of a finite graph \(G\), \[\chi_f(G)=\min\left\{\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}x_S:\sum_{S\ni v}x_S\ge1,\ x_S\ge0\right\}=\max\left\{\sum_{v\in V}y_v:\sum_{v\in S}y_v\le1\ (S\in\mathcal S),\ y_v\ge0\right\}.\] Every integral coloring is a feasible integral stable-set cover, so \(\chi_f(G)\le\chi(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractional coloring is the LP relaxation of covering vertices by stable sets, dual to packing vertex weights bounded on every stable set.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) is the family of all stable sets of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\chi_f(G)=\min\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}x_S=\max\sum_{v\in V}y_v\le\chi(G)\) under the displayed constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Coloring Stable-Set Duality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Theta sandwich linking independent-set SDP bounds to coloring bounds through complementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite simple graph \(G\), the Lovász theta number satisfies \(\alpha(G)\le\vartheta(G)\le\chi(\overline G)\). Equivalently, \(\alpha(\overline G)\le\vartheta(\overline G)\le\chi(G)\). Thus \(\vartheta(G)\) upper-bounds the independence number and \(\vartheta(\overline G)\) lower-bounds the chromatic number.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Theta of a graph bounds its independence number, while theta of its complement lower-bounds its chromatic number.
knowledge_statements.title: Lovász Theta Coloring–Stability Sandwich
Coloring–Stable-Set Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality relation connecting proper colorings and independent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite simple graph with \(n=|V|>0\). Every color class of a proper coloring is an independent set and therefore has cardinality at most \(\alpha(G)\). Hence any proper coloring using \(q\) colors satisfies \(n\le q\alpha(G)\). Minimizing over proper colorings gives
\[\chi(G)\ge \left\lceil\frac{n}{\alpha(G)}\right\rceil,\qquad \alpha(G)\chi(G)\ge n.\]
Together with \(\alpha(G)\le\vartheta(G)\), this explains the interface between independent-set SDP bounds and lower bounds sought for graph coloring.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Color classes are independent sets, so every proper coloring needs at least the ceiling of n divided by the independence number colors.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite nonempty simple graph.

Hence a fixed vector-chromatic value does not bound the number of colors required on unrestricted graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kneser graphs KG(3r,r) have vector chromatic number three but unbounded ordinary chromatic number.
assumptions_latex: Vertices of \(KG(3r,r)\) are the \(r\)-subsets of \([3r]\), with disjoint sets adjacent.

Coloring Relaxation Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Odd cycles exhibit an integrality gap for vector chromatic relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the odd cycle \(C_{2m+1}\) with \(m\ge2\), its chromatic number is \(\chi(C_{2m+1})=3\), whereas its vector chromatic number satisfies
\[\chi_v(C_{2m+1})=1+\sec\!\left(\frac{\pi}{2m+1}\right)<3.\]
Here \(\chi_v(G)\) is the least real \(t\ge2\) for which unit vectors \(v_u\) exist with \(\langle v_u,v_v\rangle\le-1/(t-1)\) on every edge. Thus feasibility of the vector-coloring SDP below three does not certify bipartiteness and cannot by itself be rounded to a coloring using the ceiling of its value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Odd cycles have chromatic number three but vector chromatic value below three, preventing exact color recovery from the basic vector relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The vector chromatic number uses the displayed edge-inner-product convention.

Integrality of \(\widehat x\) alone implies neither satisfaction of additional hard constraints nor an approximation ratio. Such conclusions require a predicate- and relaxation-specific bound such as \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{val}(\widehat x)]\ge \alpha\operatorname{SDP}(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Producing an integral labeling alone supplies neither hard-constraint feasibility nor an approximation guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite CSP instance over \([q]\).
\(\mathcal R\) always returns a labeling in \([q]^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gaussian Hyperplane Rounding for Even Boolean Two-CSPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correlation-preserving rounding for Boolean binary predicates invariant under simultaneous sign reversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose every predicate has the form \(P_{ij}(s,t)=a_{ij}+d_{ij}st\). Given feasible unit vectors \(v_i\), draw \(g\sim N(0,I)\) and set \(\widehat x_i=\operatorname{sign}\langle g,v_i\rangle\), using a fixed convention at zero. Then
\[\mathbb E[\widehat x_i\widehat x_j]=\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin\langle v_i,v_j\rangle,\]
and therefore
\[\mathbb E[P_{ij}(\widehat x_i,\widehat x_j)]=a_{ij}+\frac{2d_{ij}}{\pi}\arcsin\langle v_i,v_j\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared Gaussian hyperplane rounds unit vectors to Boolean labels, with pair correlations given by the arcsine identity.
assumptions_latex: All rounded vectors are unit vectors in one Euclidean space.
Every predicate is invariant under simultaneous sign reversal.
The Gaussian direction is standard and isotropic.
knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Hyperplane Rounding for Even Boolean Two-CSPs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-moment and pair-correlation SDP relaxation for weighted Boolean binary predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let labels be \(x_i\in\{-1,1\}\), and write each binary predicate uniquely as \(P_{ij}(s,t)=a_{ij}+b_{ij}s+c_{ij}t+d_{ij}st\). Introduce unit vectors \(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_n\) and maximize
\[\sum_{ij}w_{ij}\bigl(a_{ij}+b_{ij}\langle v_0,v_i\rangle+c_{ij}\langle v_0,v_j\rangle+d_{ij}\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\bigr)\]
subject to their Gram matrix being positive semidefinite with unit diagonal. Every integral assignment embeds as \(v_i=x_i v_0\), so the SDP optimum upper-bounds the maximum integral value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean first moments and pair products are replaced by entries of a positive-semidefinite unit-diagonal Gram matrix.
assumptions_latex: The instance has Boolean labels and weighted predicates of arity at most two.

notation.meaning: Reference vector representing the constant Boolean value one.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Two-CSP Vector Relaxation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation guarantee for Boolean equality and inequality predicates under the correlation SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider weighted constraints \(x_ix_j=b_{ij}\), where \(b_{ij}\in\{-1,1\}\), with SDP contribution \((1+b_{ij}\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)/2\). Shared-Gaussian hyperplane rounding satisfies \[\mathbb E[\operatorname{val}(\widehat x)]\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{SDP},\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}=\min_{-1\le t<1}\frac{(2/\pi)\arccos(t)}{1-t}.\] Consequently it is an \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\)-approximation for weighted Max-2-LIN over \(\mathbb Z_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared hyperplane rounding achieves the Goemans–Williamson factor for weighted Boolean equality and inequality constraints.
assumptions_latex: The SDP uses unit vectors and the stated correlation objective.

notation.meaning: Required parity sign for constraint ij.

knowledge_statements.title: Max-2-LIN Hyperplane Approximation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of the inference from integral output to satisfaction of designated hard predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two Boolean variables with the hard predicate \(x_1=x_2\). If a rounding rule outputs \(\widehat x_1,\widehat x_2\) independently and uniformly from \(\{-1,1\}\), it always produces an integral labeling but violates the hard predicate with probability \(1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent integral labels violate a hard equality constraint with probability one half.
assumptions_latex: The equality predicate is designated as a hard constraint.
The two rounded labels are independent and uniform on \(\{-1,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Integral-Labeling Hard-Constraint Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Label-vector relaxation for weighted binary predicates over a finite domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a weighted two-CSP over labels \([q]\), introduce a unit vector \(v_0\) and vectors \(v_{i,a}\) whose Gram matrix is positive semidefinite, satisfying
\[\sum_{a=1}^qv_{i,a}=v_0,\qquad \langle v_{i,a},v_{i,b}\rangle=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \langle v_{i,a},v_{j,b}\rangle\ge0.\]
Maximize
\[\sum_{(i,j)}w_{ij}\sum_{a,b\in[q]}P_{ij}(a,b)\langle v_{i,a},v_{j,b}\rangle.\]
Every integral labeling embeds by taking \(v_{i,x_i}=v_0\) and all other label vectors zero, so the SDP optimum upper-bounds the integral optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Label indicators are replaced by orthogonal label vectors whose cross inner products act as pairwise pseudo-probabilities.
assumptions_latex: The instance has finite label set \([q]\), nonnegative constraint weights, and predicates of arity at most two.
The displayed vectors have a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix.

notation.meaning: Vector representing assignment of label a to variable i.

knowledge_statements.title: Basic Finite-Domain Two-CSP SDP

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gaussian Threshold Rounding with Prescribed Boolean Marginals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Biased Boolean rounding preserving SDP first moments; no predicate-independent approximation factor is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given unit vectors \(v_0,v_i\), put \(\mu_i=\langle v_0,v_i\rangle\). For \(|\mu_i|<1\), define \(u_i=(v_i-\mu_i v_0)/\sqrt{1-\mu_i^2}\), draw \(g\sim N(0,I)\) in \(v_0^\perp\), and set \(\widehat x_i=1\) iff \(\langle g,u_i\rangle\le\Phi^{-1}((1+\mu_i)/2)\). For \(\mu_i\in\{-1,1\}\), set \(\widehat x_i=\mu_i\). Then \(\Pr[\widehat x_i=1]=(1+\mu_i)/2\) and \(\mathbb E[\widehat x_i]=\mu_i\); joint probabilities are the corresponding correlated Gaussian threshold probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correlated Gaussian thresholds chosen from SDP biases preserve every Boolean marginal.
assumptions_latex: \(v_0\) and every \(v_i\) are unit vectors in one Euclidean space.

notation.meaning: SDP first moment of variable i.
Normalized component of v_i orthogonal to v_0.

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Threshold Rounding with Prescribed Boolean Marginals

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Domain Moment SDP for Higher-Arity CSPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-2t pseudoexpectation relaxation for predicates of arity at most t.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Encode labels by indicators \(z_{i,a}\) satisfying \(z_{i,a}^2=z_{i,a}\), \(z_{i,a}z_{i,b}=0\) for \(a\ne b\), and \(\sum_a z_{i,a}=1\). A degree-\(2t\) pseudoexpectation \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}\) satisfies \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}[1]=1\), \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}[p^2]\ge0\) for \(\deg p\le t\), and every degree-compatible multiple of the indicator identities. Maximizing the pseudoexpectation of the weighted predicate polynomials is an SDP relaxation and upper-bounds the integral optimum when predicate arity is at most \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive pseudoexpectation satisfying finite-domain indicator identities relaxes higher-arity CSP assignments.
assumptions_latex: Every predicate has arity at most \(t\).

notation.meaning: Indicator for assigning label a to variable i.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Moment SDP for Higher-Arity CSPs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Best-of-Repetitions Amplification from an Expected CSP Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Confidence amplification for a bounded maximization-CSP rounding theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the value returned by one independent rounding run, with \(0\le X\le\operatorname{OPT}\) and \(\mathbb E[X]\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\), where \(0\le\alpha<1\). For \(0<\varepsilon\le\alpha\), put \(p=\Pr[X\ge(\alpha-\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}]\). Then \(p\ge\varepsilon/(1-\alpha+\varepsilon)\). Consequently, the best of \(r\) independent runs satisfies \[\Pr[X_{\mathrm{best}}\ge(\alpha-\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}]\ge1-\exp\!\left(-\frac{r\varepsilon}{1-\alpha+\varepsilon}\right).\] Thus failure probability at most \(\delta\) follows when \(r\ge((1-\alpha+\varepsilon)/\varepsilon)\ln(1/\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining the best independent run converts a bounded expected approximation into a slightly weaker high-probability guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The rounding runs are mutually independent.

notation.meaning: Objective value from one rounded assignment.
Largest objective value among the repeated runs.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-of-Repetitions Amplification from an Expected CSP Guarantee

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic realization of product rounding when conditional values are computable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix variables sequentially. For each possible label of the current variable, evaluate the conditional expected final objective while later variables retain their product marginals, and choose a maximizing label. The final assignment \(x\) satisfies \[\operatorname{val}(x)\ge\mathbb E[\operatorname{val}(\widehat x)].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedily preserving conditional expectation derandomizes independent CSP rounding.
assumptions_latex: All required conditional expectations can be computed or safely compared.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Expectation Derandomization of Product Rounding

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent Rounding from Singleton CSP Marginals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Baseline finite-domain product rounding using singleton marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(p_{i,a}\ge0\) with \(\sum_a p_{i,a}=1\), independently set \(\widehat x_i=a\) with probability \(p_{i,a}\). For a constraint \(C\) on \(S_C\), \[\mathbb E[P_C(\widehat x_{S_C})]=\sum_{a\in[q]^{S_C}}P_C(a)\prod_{i\in S_C}p_{i,a_i}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent sampling from singleton marginals has an explicit product-distribution objective formula.
assumptions_latex: The CSP and label set \([q]\) are finite.

notation.meaning: Singleton marginal for label a at variable i.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Rounding from Singleton CSP Marginals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation size and qualified weak-optimization complexity of the recorded finite-domain moment relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=nq\) be the number of label-indicator variables. A degree-\(2t\) moment relaxation has at most \(\sum_{j=0}^{2t}\binom{N+j-1}{j}=N^{O(t)}\) indexed moments and a moment matrix of order at most \(\sum_{j=0}^{t}\binom{N+j-1}{j}=N^{O(t)}\). Hence its explicit formulation has polynomial size for fixed \(q,t\). For rational bounded data, under the regularity assumptions required by weak SDP optimization, additive accuracy \(\eta\) is obtainable in time polynomial in the formulation size, input bit length, and \(\log(1/\eta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-level finite-domain moment SDP has polynomial formulation size, with an exponent increasing with the level.
assumptions_latex: The CSP has \(n\) variables and domain size \(q\).
The weak-optimization claim assumes rational bounded data and the required SDP regularity.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Level Moment-SDP Formulation Size
Constraint-Satisfaction Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian maximum-score rounding for label-vector SDP solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For variables \(i\in[n]\) with label set \([q]\), suppose an SDP solution supplies vectors \(v_{i,a}\) for every label \(a\in[q]\). Draw independent standard Gaussian vectors \(g_1,\ldots,g_q\) in their common ambient space and set
\[\widehat x_i\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{a\in[q]}\langle g_a,v_{i,a}\rangle,\]
using a fixed tie rule. Output \(\widehat x\in[q]^n\) and evaluate each constraint predicate on its rounded labels. Repeating the rounding independently and retaining the assignment of greatest objective value converts the vector relaxation into a feasible constraint-satisfaction assignment without decreasing the best observed value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round each variable to the label whose SDP vector receives the largest independent Gaussian score, then retain the best repeated assignment.
assumptions_latex: All vectors \(v_{i,a}\) lie in one finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
Every constraint predicate is evaluable on assignments in \([q]^n\).
The number of repetitions is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x\in[q]^n\) is a feasible integral labeling for the CSP instance.

notation.meaning: SDP vector for assigning label a to variable i.
Independent Gaussian scoring vector for label a.

children.title: Balanced Graph Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite rounding for graph partitions subject to balance requirements.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unweighted bisection is the sharp-balance specialization and is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With unit vertex weights, even \(|V|\), and \(\beta=1/2\), the balance constraints force \(|S|=|V\setminus S|=|V|/2\). The resulting minimum-bisection problem is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum bisection is the exact half-balance specialization and is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Bisection Specialization and Hardness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reporting convention separating cut-cost approximation from achieved balance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For requested balance \(\beta\), a \((\rho,\widehat\beta)\)-bicriteria guarantee returns \(\widehat S\) such that \(c(\delta(\widehat S))\le\rho\,\mathrm{OPT}_\beta\) and \(\widehat\beta\mu(V)\le\mu(\widehat S)\le(1-\widehat\beta)\mu(V)\). It is an approximation for the original feasible region only when \(\widehat\beta\ge\beta\); otherwise the balance relaxation must be reported separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bicriteria guarantee separately records cost approximation and the balance actually achieved.

notation.meaning: Optimum under the requested balance constraint

knowledge_statements.title: Bicriteria Balance Guarantees

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset-weight feasibility boundary for the discrete balanced-cut problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Writing \(M=\mu(V)>0\), a \(\beta\)-balanced cut exists exactly when some proper nonempty subset \(S\subset V\) satisfies \(\beta M\le\mu(S)\le(1-\beta)M\). In particular, if one vertex has weight greater than \((1-\beta)M\), no feasible balanced cut exists. With unit weights and even \(|V|\), the exact bisection constraint is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted balance can make the problem infeasible; an excessively heavy vertex is a simple obstruction.
knowledge_statements.title: Balance Feasibility Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vector SDP Relaxation for Weighted Balanced Cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic sign-vector SDP relaxation retaining the requested weighted balance interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=\mu(V)\). Introduce unit vectors \(v_u\) and minimize \[\frac14\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E}c_{uv}\|v_u-v_v\|_2^2\] subject to \[\left\|\sum_{u\in V}\mu_u v_u\right\|_2^2\le(1-2\beta)^2M^2.\] An integral cut embeds as \(v_u=z_ue\), \(z_u\in\{-1,1\}\); its objective equals \(c(\delta(S))\), and its vector constraint is equivalent to \(|\mu(S)-\mu(V\setminus S)|\le(1-2\beta)M\). Thus the SDP optimum lower-bounds the minimum \(\beta\)-balanced cut cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace cut signs by unit vectors and relax squared weighted imbalance while preserving integral cut costs.

notation.meaning: Unit SDP vector assigned to vertex u.

knowledge_statements.title: Vector SDP Relaxation for Weighted Balanced Cut

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional certificate linking a feasible rounded cut to an SDP lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\le\operatorname{OPT}_\beta\) be the value of a certified feasible SDP relaxation. If a displayed set \(S\) satisfies \(\beta\mu(V)\le\mu(S)\le(1-\beta)\mu(V)\) and \(c(\delta(S))\le\rho L\), then \(S\) is a feasible \(\rho\)-approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A balanced cut costing at most rho times a certified SDP lower bound is a certified rho-approximation.
review_flags: If the achieved balance is below \(\beta\), this does not certify feasibility for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced-Cut SDP Approximation Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Binary Cut Formulation with Weighted Balance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact mixed-integer representation of weighted two-way balanced graph partitioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(z_v\in\{0,1\}\) and \(t_{uv}\ge0\) for every edge. Impose \(t_{uv}\ge z_u-z_v\), \(t_{uv}\ge z_v-z_u\), and \(\beta M\le\sum_v\mu_vz_v\le(1-\beta)M\), where \(M=\sum_v\mu_v\). Minimizing \(\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E}c_{uv}t_{uv}\) is exactly weighted \(\beta\)-balanced graph partitioning; an optimum may be chosen with \(t_{uv}=|z_u-z_v|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary side indicators, edge-disagreement variables, and a weighted balance interval give an exact balanced-cut formulation.

notation.meaning: Indicator that vertex v lies on the selected side

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Cut Formulation with Weighted Balance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual of the Basic Weighted Balanced-Cut SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix dual and exact-arithmetic lower-bound certificate for the accepted basic vector relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=\sum_u\mu_u\), \(B=(1-2\beta)M\), \(K=\frac12\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E}c_{uv}\), let \(H_{uv}=H_{vu}=-c_{uv}/4\) on edges and zero otherwise, and let \(W=\mu\mu^\top\). The Gram formulation is \[\min\{K+\langle H,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ X_{uu}=1,\ \langle W,X\rangle\le B^2\}.\] An equivalent dual is \[\max_{y\in\mathbb R^V,\lambda\ge0}\left\{K-\sum_uy_u-\lambda B^2:H+\operatorname{Diag}(y)+\lambda W\succeq0\right\}.\] Every dual-feasible pair supplies the displayed lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagonal vector and nonnegative balance multiplier with a positive-semidefinite slack matrix certify a lower bound for the basic balanced-cut SDP.
